300024744.scope: Pincerlike hand tools with scissors action, usually with serrated jaws; used for gripping, holding, bending, and cutting.

300024758.label: brooms (maintenance tools)
300024758.scope: Tools for sweeping. Originally made of twigs fixed to a handle; now refers to handled tools with bristles made of any material.

300024760.label: brushes (implements)
300024760.scope: Implements consisting of bristles, hair, or the like, set in or attached to a handle; used for painting, cleaning, polishing, or grooming.

300024788.label: piercing tools
300024788.scope: Tools used to penetrate materials, such as awls.

300024809.label: files (tools)
300024809.scope: Steel hand tools with teeth or raised oblique ridges; used for scraping, redressing, or smoothing metal or wood.

300024814.label: molds (shaping equipment)
300024814.scope: Hollow forms in which castings or pressings are made; used with many materials, including clay, metal, glass, and paper.

300024823.label: hammers (tools)
300024823.scope: Hand tools having a hard solid head, usually of metal or stone, set transversely on a handle. They are used for driving nails, beating, breaking, or other applications involving pounding or striking. The term may also refer to machines in which a heavy block of metal is used for the same purpose.

300024841.label: tools
300024841.scope: Objects, especially those hand-held, for performing or facilitating mechanical operations.

300024860.label: projectile points
300024860.scope: Pieces of hard material, typically stone or metal, sharpened to have a cutting edge or penetrating point for use as projectiles or the heads of projectile weapons.

300024917.label: blades (tool and equipment components)
300024917.scope: The sharpened, flat-edged cutting part of a tool or weapon.

300024970.label: shafts (tool components)
300024970.scope: Long, straight parts of various types of tools, machines, and weapons, such as the rods that transmit power or motion from one part of a machine to another, or the slender sticks that constitute the main bodies of arrows.

300025375.label: coopers
300025375.scope: Persons who make or repair wooden vessels formed of staves and hoops, such as casks, buckets, tubs. Also shipboard artisans who repair casks and other containers.

300026378.label: primers (books)
300026378.scope: Elementary books for teaching children to read.

300026459.label: breviaries
300026459.scope: Religious books typically containing collections of prayers, psalms, readings, and rites.The form first appeared in the 11th century Christian monastic communities and among clerics, although the texts of the longer Divine Office had been established in the Roman rite by the 7th century and in Carolingian Europe by the 10th century. Although it was a complex book, it was briefer than the full Divine Office, thus known as a "breviary." The "book of hours" was developed by the 13th century as an even less complex book of prayers for the lay community. Works similar to the Christian breviary were adapted from primary texts of other faiths, including the Koran and Hindu works; these works are also referred to as breviaries. Breviaries may contain elaborate illumination.

300026472.label: missals
300026472.scope: Books containing all the Roman Catholic prayers and responses necessary for celebrating the mass throughout the year.

300026476.label: prayer books
300026476.scope: Books containing prayers and other forms of worship.

300026705.label: almanacs
300026705.scope: Publications, usually annuals, containing a variety of useful facts of miscellaneous nature, or statistical information; originally included projections of coming days, months, and holidays.

300026741.label: calendars (documents)
300026741.scope: Registers of days or other contrivances for reckoning days, months, years, etc., such as a table showing the division of a given year into its months, weeks, days, years, or other divisions of time. A calendar may include important astronomical data, ecclesiastical or other festivals, and other events belonging to specific days. For calendric systems of dates, see children under "<dating systems by specific type>."

300028051.label: books
300028051.scope: Items comprising a collection of leaves of paper, parchment, wood, stiffened textile, ivory, metal tablets, or other flat material, that are blank, written on, or printed, and are strung or bound together in a volume.

300028094.label: maps (documents)
300028094.scope: Refers to graphic or photogrammetric representations of the Earth's surface or a part of it, including physical features and political boundaries, where each point corresponds to a geographical or celestial position according to a definite scale or projection. The term may also refer to similar depictions of other planets, suns, other heavenly bodies, or areas of the heavens. Maps are typically depicted on a flat medium, such as on paper, a wall, or a computer screen. For similar depictions on a sphere, see "globes (cartographic spheres)."

300028442.label: world maps
300028442.scope: Maps depicting all or most of the surface of the Earth.

300028877.label: seals (artifacts)
300028877.scope: Objects bearing designs, emblems, letters, names,  words, etc. in intaglio that are used for stamping a flat surface or for making an impression in relief on some soft, tenacious substance such as clay or wax. They may be flat or cylindrical, the impression made by rolling the seal over the surface. Seals may be used to authenticate documents or for decoration.

300028879.label: tablets (information artifacts)
300028879.scope: Flat surfaces or slabs, either portable or mounted on a wall or other structure, bearing or intended to bear inscriptions or pictures; also, thin, rigid slabs used as writing surfaces.

300033260.label: hardware (components)
300033260.scope: Large and small items that are necessary to attach, anchor, hold, or join materials and components of structures, furniture, and other objects. Also, items used in the finishing of buildings and objects, such as hinges and knobs.

300033313.label: door rings
300033313.scope: Entrance doorbell devices activated by turning a bar or thumb piece located on the outside of an exterior door frame that communicates with a bell located somewhere inside the door frame.

300033367.label: hinges (hardware)
300033367.scope: Flexible plates or leaves joined by a pin so as to allow swinging motion in a single plane of one of the members to which they are attached, such as a door or gate.

300033387.label: latches
300033387.scope: Holding devices that rely on some form of horizontal bar, such as a bolt, rod, or hook as the means of closure. Distinguished from "catches" which rely on a roller, magnet, or friction.

300033407.label: locks (securing devices)
300033407.scope: Various types of securing devices used to secure openings or containers, traditionally consisting of a dead bolt or system of bolts and operated by a key or similar device, but today, by extension, may include other locking devices that may have other forms.

300033419.label: door locks
300033419.scope: Contrivances for securing doors in closed position, often with a combination of a keyed bolt.

300033537.label: hooks (fasteners)
300033537.scope: Bent or curved devices used for suspending or fastening objects or for attaching objects to a surface.

300033565.label: nails (fasteners)
300033565.scope: Fasteners that are designed for impact insertion, usually slender, pointed, and headed.

300033945.label: icons (devotional images)
300033945.scope: In general meaning, images that portray a sacred entity and that are themselves regarded as sacred. In specific meaning, the term is typically used particularly for Christian images produced in the Eastern Rite churches, since the 6th century, according to prescribed formulas of subject (Christ, the Virgin, saints, and the great feasts) and composition, for devotional use in the church or home. Most commonly comprising tempera on panel, but they may be in any two-dimensional or relief medium, including fresco. Christians who venerate icons make the distinction between veneration and worship, although in actual practice the distinction is blurred. For a non-Christian image that is sacred or embodies a deity, use "idol" or "cult image."

300036363.label: fasteners
300036363.scope: Devices that fasten or hold together separate parts.

300036406.label: lath nails
300036406.scope: Nails having a thin shank and a flat head, designed for attaching laths, which are narrow strips of wood, upon battens.

300036423.label: pins (fasteners)
300036423.scope: Small fasteners with a pointed or tapered end made of various materials used to pin something down or fasten something together. For jewelry having pins as methods of attachment, use "pins (jewelry)."

300036425.label: rivets
300036425.scope: Headed pinlike or boltlike fasteners of some malleable material used for uniting two or more pieces by passing the shank through a hole in each piece and then beating or pressing down the plain end so as to make a second head.

300036429.label: studs (bosses)
300036429.scope: Bosses, rivets, or nails with a large head for ornament or protection.

300036430.label: tacks
300036430.scope: Small, sharp-pointed nail-like fasteners of iron or brass with a comparatively large head and used for fastening a light or thin object to something more solid.

300036745.label: armor
300036745.scope: Refers generally to that category of costume designed to be worn or carried to protect the body in combat. Armor pieces which are always physical parts of or are affixed to other pieces and cannot function alone are collocated under the guide term "<armor components>." For specifically groups of armor pieces designed as a whole to possess particular physical characteristics in order to suit a particular purpose or occasion, see "armors."

300036746.label: body armor
300036746.scope: Pieces of armor worn on the human body.

300036756.label: aventails
300036756.scope: Tippets of mail attached around the lower edge and face opening of helmets, commonly basnets, to protect the shoulders, neck, and part of the face; used in the 14th and 15th centuries.

300036760.label: cuisses
300036760.scope: Plate armor for the thighs, usually attached to the poleyns at their lower end. Introduced during the 14th century, they evolved from a single plate covering the front of the thigh to articulated lames encircling the entire thigh.

300036768.label: cuirasses
300036768.scope: Armor protecting the front and back of the torso, variously made throughout their history of layers of linen or leather, metal scales, lames, or plates, or combinations of leather and metal.

300036772.label: gauntlets
300036772.scope: Gloves made of cloth or leather having a deep cuff which covers part of the forearm. Styled after those worn as armor.

300036794.label: helmets (protective wear)
300036794.scope: Any of various forms of protective coverings for the head, usually made of a hard material, including the outside steel layer of helmets that consist of inner and outer parts.

300036802.label: basnets
300036802.scope: Helmets, generally ogival or egg-shaped with a pointed apex, and often fitted with an aventail and a hinged or pivoted visor, usually a pig-faced visor; used from the 13th to the 15th century. In the 15th century they became more globular and the aventail was replaced by gorget plates.

300036811.label: helms (body armor)
300036811.scope: Heavy helmets completely enclosing the head and face, originally flat-topped, later having a conical or rounded top; used in warfare from the late 12th to the mid-14th century, and continued in use in tournaments until the mid-16th century.

300036813.label: morions
300036813.scope: Open helmets developed in the 16th century from the kettle hat, consisting of a skull with a broad curved brim, flat or turned down at the sides but sweeping upwards into a peak at front and rear.

300036863.label: lance rests
300036863.scope: Devices attached to the right side of the breastplate, generally consisting of a small base plate to which is fixed or hinged a short, stout, projecting arm on which to rest the lance. They served to distribute the shock of impact.

300036869.label: shields (armor)
300036869.scope: General term for armor pieces carried in the hand or on the arm, used to parry an opponent's blows or provide shelter from projectiles. They have existed worldwide throughout history in a wide variety of sizes, shapes, and materials.

300036874.label: bucklers
300036874.scope: Small shields with an internal grip, held in the left hand during foot combat; they were used from the 13th to the 17th century.

300036879.label: targets (shields)
300036879.scope: Light shields or bucklers, borne instead of the heavy shield by targemen, footmen, archers, and sometimes horsemen. They were in common use by infantry soldiers from the 13th to the 16th century and in tournaments. They may be fitted concave to the body, fitted on the inside with two straps, the forearm passing through one and the hand grasping the other, or having a slot for placement of a weapon.

300036900.label: horse armor
300036900.scope: General term for armor to be worn by a horse. For armor worn by humans mounted on a horse, see "equestrian armors."

300036905.label: shaffrons
300036905.scope: Armor pieces for the front of a horse's or camel's head, often with side plates to protect the cheeks and often decorated to match the armor of the rider. Known in classical Greece and from the 12th century on throughout Europe, the Middle East, Turkey, North Africa, and Japan, they were commonly made of either steel or leather, though the Japanese also used papier-maché and wood, the Ottoman Turks copper, and the Sudanese mainly brass.

300036921.label: crinets
300036921.scope: Armor for the horse's neck, made of narrow lames articulated together, or of lames alternating with bands of mail.

300036923.label: spurs (costume accessories)
300036923.scope: Metal goads attached to a rider's boot heels, used to drive the horse on.

300036928.label: ammunition
300036928.scope: Projectiles and propellants used to operate firearms.

300036930.label: quivers
300036930.scope: Deep containers made of metal, wood, or leather, used for holding and carrying arrows, typically worn slung across the back.

300036939.label: serpentines (cannons)
300036939.scope: Cannons in use from the 15th to the 17th century, produced in various sizes and calibers but typically long in relation to their caliber and longer and lighter than bombards.

300036976.label: arrows (projectiles)
300036976.scope: Projectiles generally consisting of a straight, slender shaft with a sharp point or carrying a sharp edged or pointed head of stone or metal, shot from a bow. More developed versions also have flights near the butt to stabilize their trajectory.

300036982.label: axes (weapons)
300036982.scope: Cutting weapons consisting basically of a relatively heavy, flat blade fixed to a handle, wielded by either striking or throwing. For axes used for other purposes, typically having narrower blades, use "axes (tools)."

300036983.label: battle-axes
300036983.scope: Axes used in combat and warfare since prehistoric times, made in various forms and sizes from one geographic region and culture to another, but typically having a broad blade with a convex cutting edge and a handle, and wielded with one or two hands to strike cutting blows or to throw.

300036999.label: bows (weapons)
300036999.scope: Stringed projectile weapons designed to propel arrows, generally consisting of a long stave of wood, metal, fiberglass, or other flexible material, with a length of strong string fastened to the tips of the stave which is bent in a curve, either permanently or from the tension of the string. The string is drawn back, holding the arrow by means of a notch in its rear tip, and propels the arrow upon release.

300037000.label: crossbows
300037000.scope: Bows basically consisting of a curved stave mounted crosswise on a center shaft by means of a system of cord or gut bindings or metal bands, the string being drawn back, held, and released by some mechanical means such as a windlass or a rotatable nut. They were in use as early as the 11th century and continue to be used contemporarily for hunting and recreation.

300037010.label: halberds
300037010.scope: Staff weapons widely used in warfare in the 15th and 16th centuries, having an axlike blade with a short fluke on the back and a spike at the top of the staff. After the late 16th century they increasingly came to be used solely as ceremonial weapons, in which capacity they survived well into the 19th century.

300037019.label: javelins
300037019.scope: Relatively short, light throwing spears used since ancient times in warfare and in hunting large game. Use also for the light shafts with pointed metal tip thrown for distance in track and field competition.

300037029.label: lances (cavalry weapons)
300037029.scope: Staff weapons used both in warfare and tournaments, consisting of a long shaft with a steel head, carried by mounted knights or light cavalry.

300037032.label: partisans
300037032.scope: Staff weapons having a broad, tapering triangular blade with two upturned lugs or wings at the base, used as thrusting and cutting weapons but also extremely popular as ceremonial weapons from the 16th to the 19th century, and still occasionally used as such today.

300037033.label: pikes (spears)
300037033.scope: Use generally for spears having a very sharply pointed steel head, somtimes with a hook or pick on the side. Use particularly for the very long type, from 16 to 22 feet in length, having a small leaf- or lozenge-shaped head, used by infantry as a defense against cavalry from the late 15th to the mid-17th century.

300037038.label: spears (weapons)
300037038.scope: Simple staff weapons having a sharp-pointed head and no auxiliary blades or points, used both in warfare and hunting since ancient times in many cultures and regions. Various forms have been designed for thrusting or throwing or both.

300037048.label: swords
300037048.scope: Edged weapons consisting basically of a blade, generally longer than that of daggers or knives, and a grip; designed for delivering cutting or thrusting blows or both.

300037058.label: daggers (weapons)
300037058.scope: Weapons with a short, double-edged, sharp-pointed blade and a grip, used for stabbing or parrying.

300037062.label: baselards
300037062.scope: Daggers having a hilt shaped like a capital H on its side (becoming more like a capital I over time), usually worn at the girdle by civilians. The form originated in southern Germany or Switzerland in the late 13th century and remained in wide use throughout Europe until the late 15th century. Some types are as long as short swords.

300037085.label: rapiers
300037085.scope: Light swords with a long, narrow, double-edged blade and a hilt furnished with extensive protection for the hand, such as arms of the hilt and side rings, a shell guard, or a cup guard. Originally designed for both cutting and thrusting, they developed into purely thrusting swords and became the principal fencing weapons of the 16th and 17th centuries.

300037110.label: edged weapon components
300037110.scope: Parts and components of edged weapons.

300037119.label: hilts
300037119.scope: Handles on edged weapons such as daggers, swords, and knives, typically consisting of the grip and the guard or guards, if any.

300037139.label: scabbards
300037139.scope: Rigid sheaths made of wood, metal, or leather, used to enclose and carry edged weapons or tools, or hand weapons such as carbines and rifles.

300037158.label: handguns (small arms)
300037158.scope: Firearms that can be held and fired with one hand.

300037189.label: locks (firearm components)
300037189.scope: Mechanical devices for igniting the propellant charge in firearms.

300037206.label: clubs (weapons)
300037206.scope: General term for percussive weapons typically consisting of a staff of wood, metal, or other hard, heavy material, often carrying a head of stone or metal, wielded by hand as striking weapons.

300037214.label: maces (weapons)
300037214.scope: Clubs used throughout Europe mainly from the 11th to the 17th century, made either entirely of metal or of a wooden shaft with a metal head, the head having longitudinal grooves or flanges and sometimes surmounted by a spike.

300037216.label: slings (projectile weapons)
300037216.scope: Throwing weapons consisting basically of a strap of leather, fabric, or similar flexible material, widening into a pouch at the center to hold the projectile. They are held by the two ends and swung round rapidly, then one end is released to hurl the projectile.

300037564.label: curtains (opening hangings)
300037564.scope: Hangings for windows, doorways, or other openings, usually of cloth, plastic, or another such material, that are generally finished with hems, casings, pleats, or ruffles and hung by the top edge; used for privacy, control of light and drafts, or decoration.

300037584.label: candelabras (candleholders)
300037584.scope: Candleholders with two or more arms.

300037588.label: candlesticks
300037588.scope: Candleholders with a single candle socket mounted on a support with a widened base or foot for balance; often the support is columnar in form. For candleholders with a single candle socket set on a flat saucer or traylike base, use "chambersticks."

300037589.label: sconces (lighting devices)
300037589.scope: Lighting devices designed to hang on a wall having one or more candle sockets or lamp holders; often ornamental and frequently incorporating a reflector.

300037592.label: lamps (lighting devices)
300037592.scope: Lighting devices having a vessel to contain fuel used as a source of illumination, such as grease or oil. The term also refers to relatively small -- of a size to be placed on or beside a desk or table -- household or office lighting devices that incorporate a vessel of glass or some similar material that encloses the source of illumination, whether a candle, oil, gas-jet, or incandescent wire inside a light bulb. The lamp was invented at least as early as 70,000 BCE, originally consisting of a hollowed-out rock filled with moss or some other absorbent material that was soaked with animal fat and ignited. To refer to the glass bulbs used as a component of electric lamps, use "light bulbs."

300037622.label: chandeliers (hanging lights)
300037622.scope: Lighting devices designed to hang from the roof or ceiling having two or more branches, holding candles, burners, or lamps; often ornamental.

300037647.label: lanterns (lighting devices)
300037647.scope: Lighting devices, fixed or portable, designed to protect and enclose the light source, usually with sides of glass, horn, pierced metal, paper, or other material, allowing light to emerge and often having a supporting frame, hanging device, or carrying handle. They may be purely utilitarian or decorative, sometimes having ceremonial significance.

300037652.label: torches (lighting devices)
300037652.scope: Lights consisting of an open flame emitted from a stick-like handle, usually carried by hand or mounted on a wall or pole. Torches originally consisted of a stick of resinous wood or bundles of fiber soaked with pitch, wax, resin, tallow or other flammable substance. In later usage, includes other sorts of lamps on poles that are designed to be carried like torches.

300037654.label: candles
300037654.scope: Cylindrical masses typically of tallow or wax containing a wick or loosely twisted linen or cotton threads burned to give light; made by dipping or casting in a metal mold.

300037682.label: mirrors
300037682.scope: Objects with a highly polished surface, designed to reflect images clearly. The surface is typically smooth, flat, or sometimes slightly curved, made of polished metal in ancient and medieval times, but later usually of glass with a reflective coating on one side.

300037690.label: mirror
300037690.scope: Mirrors that are framed pieces of glass with a backing of one of various substances to make them reflective, used especially with reference to those made up to the 20th century.

300037737.label: screens (furniture)
300037737.scope: Refers to furniture or built-in features in the form of an upright partition that can be used to embellish, partition, shelter, and provide privacy. Screens are often highly decorated.

300037772.label: chairs (furniture forms)
300037772.scope: Seats for one person with a back or a back and arms. Distinct from "stools" which have no back.

300038155.label: commode chairs
300038155.scope: Term generally applied to a variety of chairs fitted with a chamber pot. Use "bidets (box stools)" for box stools with a chamber pot.

300038418.label: stools (seating furniture)
300038418.scope: A seat for one person, often without a back. They were the most common type of seat furniture until the 19th century. Distinct from "benches" in that they seat only one person; usually distinguished from "chairs" in that they have no back; however, tall seating pieces at a bar or counter are called stools though they sometimes have backs. Generally made in two types; one supported on four straight legs and the other with legs arranged crosswise.

300038494.label: benches (furniture)
300038494.scope: Long seats for two or more people, with or without a back, usually of wood, but also of stone, metal, or another material. A bench is distinguished from a stool by its greater length.

300038697.label: beds (furniture)
300038697.scope: Generally, the sleeping places of humans and animals. Specifically, permanent pieces of furniture comprised of a bedstead, which is the wooden or metal support, and the bedding, including the mattress and cover.

300038847.label: cradles (children's beds)
300038847.scope: Small beds for infants, usually on bends.

300038860.label: case furniture
300038860.scope: Furniture that encloses a space and is generally boxlike in structure; intended for storage or display.

300038992.label: chests (case furniture)
300038992.scope: Large boxes with hinged lids intended for the storage of textiles, clothing, and other articles.

300039006.label: caskets (personal gear)
300039006.scope: Small chests or boxes for holding objects of value such as money, letters, and jewels; usually of wood or metal and highly ornamented and often hinged.

300039119.label: coffers (furniture)
300039119.scope: Small chests for the storage of valuables which may also serve as seats or tables.

300039124.label: trussing coffers
300039124.scope: Wood boxes, often covered in leather and tooled in gilt or bound with iron, which were used as traveling trunks to store papers, valuables, and clothes; of a type made in the late Medieval period.

300039183.label: cupboards (case furniture)
300039183.scope: General term for a closet or a cabinet enclosed by doors, often placed in a corner of a room or a recess in the wall, with shelves for keeping cups, dishes, provisions, books, or valuables. Originally boards or open structures of shelves on which cups, especially silver, might be placed for storage or display. Beginning in the 15th century, doors were added.

300039235.label: press cupboards
300039235.scope: Large, but fairly low, cupboards with both the upper and lower sections containing enclosed storage space; of a type made in 16th- and 17th-century England and 17th-century America. Distinct from "court cupboards" which have an enclosed storage cabinet above and an open shelf or shelves below.

300039338.label: desks
300039338.scope: Various forms of furniture for readers or writers, generally having a flat writing surface and often drawers and other compartments.

300039548.label: tables (support furniture)
300039548.scope: Articles of furniture consisting of a flat, slablike top supported on one or more legs or supports.

300040433.label: bedposts
300040433.scope: Upright supports on a bedstead, such as those which support the tester on a high-post bed.

300040450.label: mattresses
300040450.scope: Rectangular cases filled with yielding fabric such as cotton or hair, generally used on bedsteads.

300040453.label: testers (bed components)
300040453.scope: Rooflike components supported above the bed by posts and covering the whole area of the bed. Use "flying testers" for rooflike components generally cantilevered from the headboard and extending over the whole area of the bed. Use "half-testers" for similar forms which only extend over the head half of the bed. Use "canopies (structural elements)" for rooflike components suspended over the head of the bed by means of a cord or chain attached to the ceiling.

300041405.label: woodcuts (prints)
300041405.scope: Prints made using the process of woodcut, which is a relief process in which the design is cut into and printed from the plank side of a wood block; distinct from "wood engraving (process)," which is a relief process using the grain end of a wood block.

300041572.label: surveying instruments
300041572.scope: Tools and equipment used for conducting an examination or inspection to achieve a comprehensive view, as of a place, a situation, or an area of study, or to ascertain condition or value.

300041575.label: clocks
300041575.scope: Instruments that measure and indicate the passage of time, especially by mechanical means producing a regularly recurring action and indicating, usually by hands or changing numbers, the hours and minutes; not designed to be worn or otherwise carried about on a person. For wearable timepieces, see "watches."

300041675.label: clavichords
300041675.scope: Zitherlike instruments in the form of a rectangular box with a keyboard set in the long side. Strings, usually two per note, run from hitch pins on the left over a bridge to tuning pins at the right. Brass tangents on the rear portion of each key strike the strings from below to produce sound.

300041678.label: harpsichords
300041678.scope: Zitherlike chordophones having a keyboard which operates a plucking mechanism to sound the strings; typically of an an elongated wing shape like a grand piano with strings that run parallel to the keys.

300041684.label: virginals
300041684.scope: Small harpsichords that are usually rectangular in shape, and having one keyboard and with the strings running at right angles to the keys.

300041686.label: organs (pipe organs)
300041686.scope: Complex aerophones consisting of one or more rows of individual pipes which are made to sound by air under pressure directed from a wind-raising device and admitted to the pipes by means of valves operated from a keyboard or set of levers.

300041695.label: portative organs
300041695.scope: Small portable organs furnished with flue pipes, carried by a strap around the player's neck or shoulder; the bellows were worked by the left hand and the keyboard by the right.

300041703.label: regals
300041703.scope: Small portable organs in which the sound is produced by one or more sets of beating reeds, supplied with air from a pair of bellows and played from a keyboard.

300041729.label: drums (membranophones)
300041729.scope: Membranophones with a resonating cavity covered at one or both ends by a membrane, which is sounded by striking, rubbing, or plucking.

300041872.label: bells (idiophones)
300041872.scope: Percussion vessels consisting of a hollow object, usually of metal but in some cultures of hard clay, wood, or glass, which when struck emits a sound by the vibration of most of its mass; they are held in position at their vertex, the point farthest from their rim, and their zone of maximum vibration is towards the rim.

300041933.label: rattles (indirectly struck idiophones)
300041933.scope: Shaken idiophones made in a variety of forms worldwide, in which one or more objects strike against each other or against the inside or outside of another object.

300042020.label: citterns
300042020.scope: European wire-strung plucked lutelike chordophones played with a plectrum, very popular in the 16th and 17th centuries, having a wedge-shaped body with a curved bottom and straight shoulders narrowing towards the neck, and a low flat bridge held in position only by the strings it supports. Their most characteristic feature is a long, fretted neck which is half cut away from behind the fingerboard on the bass side, making a channel along which the player's left thumb can slide to facilitate very rapid shifts to and from high positions.

300042101.label: lutes (chordophones)
300042101.scope: Use specifically for plucked chordophones developed in the European Renaissance, having a large pear-shaped body composed of thin, narrow ribs, a flat top, central circular soundhole covered by a rose, and from seven to ten frets on the neck. For the general class of all chordophones with the plane of the strings running parallel to the resonator and a neck that serves both as string bearer and as handle, see "lutelike chordophones."

300042163.label: dulcimers
300042163.scope: Zitherlike chordophones with a box resonator and multiple strings but no keyboard, played by being struck with light hammers.

300042220.label: fiddles
300042220.scope: Refers generally for all lutelike instruments having a soundbox and played with a bow.

300042339.label: trumpets (aerophones)
300042339.scope: Generally, all lip-vibrated aerophones of predominantly cylindrical bore.

300042389.label: hunting horns
300042389.scope: Valveless lip-vibrated aerophones of conical bore, made in many shapes, originally used as signal instruments during the hunt.

300042399.label: bells (aerophone components)
300042399.scope: Flared or bulbous terminals found on many open-ended aerophone tubes.

300042405.label: bagpipes
300042405.scope: Composite reedpipes consisting of an air-tight skin, cloth, or rubber bag which serves as the air reservoir, one or more chanters with fingerholes on which the melody is played, and often one or more drone pipes which sound a continuous background to the melody. All sounding pipes have reeds and are attached to the bag by being inserted into tubular wooden stocks which are tied into openings in the bag.

300042513.label: flutes (aerophones)
300042513.scope: Generally refers to any musical wind instrument consisting of a hollow cylinder or pipe of wood, metal, or another material, with holes along its length that are stopped by the fingers or by keys that are opened by the fingers. Although most flutes are tubular, some are globular (as with a gourd flute). A flute is sounded by a stream of air from the player's lips striking against the sharp edge of an opening, breaking the air up and vibrating within the enclosed space. The air may be blown in from an end or from the side, depending upon the type of flute. Many, but not all, modern flutes are equipped with the Boehm system of keywork.

300042551.label: recorders (flutes)
300042551.scope: Family of fipple flutes that originated in Europe, traditionally made of wood, recently sometimes of plastic, with seven fingerholes and a thumb hole. Recorders may be made in several sizes, including the following: garklein, sopranino, Soprano, alto, voice flute, tenor, bass, great bass, contrabass, sub-great bass, and sub-contrabass.

300042576.label: Jew's harps
300042576.scope: Generic term for a type of mouth-resonated instrument consisting of a flexible tongue fixed at one end to a surrounding frame. The free end of the tongue is placed in front of the player's mouth cavity and is plucked with a finger.

300042695.label: tabor pipes
300042695.scope: Fipple flutes played in ensemble with the small drums called tabors, held and played by the left hand while the tabor is played by the right.

300042706.label: whistles
300042706.scope: Short, usually high-pitched duct flutes having no fingerholes, or no more than one; the body may contain a captive pellet to add a roll to the sound.

300042946.label: bowls (object components)
300042946.scope: Rounded, cuplike, hollow parts of objects, such as the body of a stemmed vessel or the part of a pipe in which tobacco is burned.

300042964.label: porringers (dishes)
300042964.scope: Small, shallow, flat-bottomed bowls or basins, often of earthenware, metal, or wood and typically having a single handle, used for soup, stews, or similar dishes. A traditional design uses one horizontal pierced handle flush with the rim. Sometimes made in pairs or sets and varying in size.

300042973.label: dishes (vessels for food)
300042973.scope: Any of various broad, relatively shallow, open vessels with a flat bottom, concave sides, and nearly level rim, sometimes having a cover; made of pottery, glass, metal, wood or another material and used especially for holding or serving food. In modern usage it is typically reserved for vessels at a dining table used for serving or holding food other than the round, flat or very shallow object used by the person dining, which is called a "plate"; however, formerly the plate was also called a "dish."

300042983.label: pans (containers)
300042983.scope: Metal, earthenware, or plastic containers, generally for domestic use, that are usually broad, shallow and open.

300042984.label: frying pans (cookware)
300042984.scope: Shallow, metal pans with a relatively long, single handle used for frying foods; sometimes made with a lid.

300042991.label: plates (general, dishes)
300042991.scope: Shallow, usually circular dishes from which food is eaten.

300043030.label: pepper casters
300043030.scope: Casters intended primarily for serving ground pepper, particularly in historical and formal usage. Pepper casters are usually of baluster or cylindrical shape, often of silver, other precious material, or porcelain; they have a finely pierced domed cover which was sometimes screwed to the container. They were often part of a set of casters that was positioned upon a special tray at table. For similar items used to sprinkle pepper, but forming one of a set of only two with a saltshaker, particularly in modern usage and when made of more modest materials and intended for daily use in a household or restaurant, use "pepper shakers"; however, usage overlaps.

300043035.label: cruets (condiment vessels)
300043035.scope: Vessels, usually with a handle and a stopper, used to serve condiments; generally of glass and often made in sets of two or more.

300043053.label: platters (carrying dishes)
300043053.scope: Large, shallow dishes, usually oval and having a ledge and a well, used for carrying other dishes.

300043062.label: salts (condiment vessels)
300043062.scope: Containers for holding table salt; made in a great variety of forms, styles, sizes and materials.  Whenever possible use a more specific term.

300043071.label: trays
300043071.scope: Open, variously shaped containers of wood, metal or other rigid material with a flat bottom and a low rim for holding, carrying, or exhibiting articles.

300043078.label: trenchers (dishes)
300043078.scope: Circular or rectangular flat dishes, generally made of wood, pottery or metal, on which meat or other food is carved or served. Early wooden examples often have a depressed area for food and a second smaller cavity for salt. Use "chargers" for large platters, usually circular or oval and often made of earthenware or metal, used for serving meat.

300043099.label: forks (flatware)
300043099.scope: Articles of flatware having a handle with a shank terminating in two or more tines, used to manipulate food especially in serving and eating.

300043149.label: spoons
300043149.scope: Utensils consisting of a shallow bowl with a handle used for preparing, cooking, serving, or eating food.

300043198.label: beakers (drinking vessels)
300043198.scope: Refers to many varieties of relatively large drinking vessels without handles, cylindrical or conical in shape, with a flat base in the form of an open cup or goblet. Specifically, in archaeology refers to the tall wide-mouthed vessels produced by the Bell Beaker culture and found in certain early Bronze Age graves.

300043202.label: cups (drinking vessels)
300043202.scope: Open bowl-shaped vessels, used chiefly for drinking, often having one handle, but sometimes two handles or none, generally on a low foot-ring; also includes similar bowl-shaped vessels, generally without handles, resting on a stem and supported by a spreading foot. Occasionally made with a lid.

300043229.label: drinking horns
300043229.scope: Drinking vessels made of horn, especially those elaborately mounted in bronze or silver.

300043230.label: drinking glasses
300043230.scope: Vessels intended for an individual to use for drinking wine, water, or other beverage.

300043236.label: goblets
300043236.scope: Drinking glasses with a large bowl, of various shapes, resting on a stemmed foot.

300044039.label: felt work
300044039.scope: Visual works made primarily of felt, which is a dense textile constructed usually of wool and fur fibers that are held together by heat, moisture, and pressure without weaving or spinning. The term is usually reserved for artistic or decorative works having felt as the medium and support (if any); clothing made of felt is not called "felt work."

300044045.label: goldwork (visual works)
300044045.scope: Visual works or parts of works made of the metal gold or of threads or another material covered in gold.

300044074.label: wickerwork (visual works)
300044074.scope: Visual works created with real or simulated flexible twigs, osiers, canes, or the like that are woven and plaited together. Examples of wickerwork are baskets and furniture.

300045514.label: jet (coal)
300045514.scope: A dense, black, semiprecious form of lignite that takes a brilliant polish and is used ornamentally, particularly in Victorian mourning jewelry.

300045614.label: basins (vessels)
300045614.scope: Open, rounded vessels of greater width than depth, with sloping or curving sides, used for receiving running water or holding water and other liquids, especially for washing purposes.

300045627.label: bottles
300045627.scope: Vessels having a neck and mouth considerably narrower than the body, used for packaging and containing liquid and dry preparations. For vessels having wider necks and mouths, use "jars."

300045643.label: boxes (containers)
300045643.scope: Rigid, often rectangular containers usually with a lid or cover in which something nonliquid is kept or carried.

300045659.label: cases (containers)
300045659.scope: A receptacle, holder, box, chest, bag, sheath, or covering fitted to contain or enclose something else; typically used for transporting or protecting the enclosed item or items.

300045666.label: ewers (vessels)
300045666.scope: Tall, wide-mouthed vessels, generally having a pouring lip, and that have a deep bowl on a stemmed base and a single vertical handle. The bowl is usually cylindrical, baluster-shaped, or helmet-shaped.

300045671.label: flasks (bottles)
300045671.scope: Spheroidal, bulbous shape, pear-shaped, or flattened vessels with a narrow neck and a small mouth, usually of glass, ceramic, metal, animal skin, wicker, or another material and used for various purposes. Also used specifically for distinctive narrow-necked vessels, usually of glass, having a rounded body, used in laboratories.

300045685.label: jugs (vessels)
300045685.scope: Vessels, generally made of earthenware, stoneware or porcelain and often of large capacity, which have a narrow neck and a handle (usually a vertical loop or scroll handle); may sometimes have a pouring lip.

300045695.label: pails
300045695.scope: Typically cylindrical or nearly cylindrical vessels, generally of metal or plastic, for catching, holding, or carrying liquids or solids and usually having a bail handle or other handle and sometimes a removable cover.

300045697.label: pots (containers)
300045697.scope: Cylindrical or rounded containers, often of metal or earthenware and varying in size; used chiefly for domestic purposes.

300045712.label: lids (covers)
300045712.scope: Covers for the opening at the top of a vessel or other receptacle, or which close the mouth of an aperture; lids may be detached or turned upon a hinge in order to give access to the interior.

300045991.label: bracelets (jewelry)
300045991.scope: Ornamental bands or circlets worn on the lower arm.  Use "armlets" for similar articles worn on the upper arm.

300045995.label: brooches
300045995.scope: Ornamental jewelry made in a variety of forms fastened by a pin. For decorative items, similar in appearance to a brooch, but attached to a garment with a spring fastening, use "clips (jewelry)."

300046012.label: rings (finger jewelry)
300046012.scope: Small circular bands worn on the finger; typically circlets of real or simulated precious metal, and frequently set with precious stones or imitations of these, intended for wearing upon the finger either as an ornament or as a token.

300046023.label: headdresses
300046023.scope: Elaborate coverings or objects for the head, especially those worn for ceremonial or ornamental purposes.

300046040.label: bodkins (hairpins)
300046040.scope: Long, single-pronged accessories used to keep hair or headgear in place or for decorative purposes.

300046057.label: boots (footwear)
300046057.scope: Footwear, the leg of which extends above the ankle joint.

300046065.label: shoes (footwear)
300046065.scope: Footwear with a relatively stiff sole and heel, and generally covering the foot at or below the ankle joint.

300046066.label: clogs
300046066.scope: Footwear made partly or wholly of wood, with a thick sole usually of wood, but sometimes of leather or cork; originally to protect the foot, hosiery, or other footwear. The term "clogs" may also apply to shoes in the style of wooden clogs, but made of other materials. For overshoes consisting of a sole set on bands of iron, use "pattens."

300046083.label: slippers (shoes)
300046083.scope: Light footwear made for indoor wear, generally without means of fastening and made to be easily slipped on and off the foot.

300046087.label: socks
300046087.scope: Hosiery that covers the foot and extends to somewhere below the knee.

300046088.label: stockings
300046088.scope: Hosiery that covers the foot and extends to the knee or above; can be heavy or lightweight.

300046091.label: berets
300046091.scope: Soft, flat-topped, visorless caps with a tight-fitting headband; in a military context, worn as an official item of headgear.

300046094.label: caps (headgear)
300046094.scope: Brimless head coverings, often made with a visor.

300046106.label: hats
300046106.scope: Shaped coverings for the head having a brim and crown, or one of the two.

300046121.label: hoods (headgear)
300046121.scope: Soft coverings for the head and neck, and sometimes extending to the shoulders, either separate or attached to a garment.

300046122.label: kerchiefs
300046122.scope: Square or triangular headcloths worn as a covering for the head.

300046128.label: veils (headcloths)
300046128.scope: Thin and lightweight coverings worn over the head or face, and sometimes extending to the shoulders, for ornament, protection, or concealment; also, similar coverings made as component parts of headgear.

300046135.label: breeches (trousers)
300046135.scope: Knee-length trousers commonly worn by men and boys in the 17th, 18th, and early 19th centuries.

300046140.label: capes (outerwear)
300046140.scope: Sleeveless outer garments of varying lengths, fastening at the neck and falling loosely from the shoulders that function as either separate garments or attach to longer coats or cloaks.

300046142.label: cloaks
300046142.scope: Sleeveless outer garments which fasten at the neck and fall loosely from the shoulders to cover the entire body; may have a yoke or some shaping from the neck to the shoulders.

300046143.label: coats (garments)
300046143.scope: Main garments usually fitted to the upper body, extending below the hip line, open at the front or side and generally having sleeves. Also, similar outer garments worn for warmth or protection from the weather.

300046161.label: gowns
300046161.scope: Long garments for women, typically cut with flowing lines. Examples include semi-fitted women's dresses worn from the Middle Ages forward, and more formal dresses of modern times. Use "robes" for long, loose garments that tend to be one piece and open down the front, not necessarily women's fashion.

300046167.label: jackets (short coats)
300046167.scope: Short coats for the upper body made in various forms and lengths, but usually no lower than the waist or upper hip; worn indoors or for light warmth and protection from the weather.

300046230.label: purse
300046230.scope: Relatively small, flat, often folding containers, typically of leather, designed with slits, pockets, and compartments for carrying paper money, credit cards, driver's license, and coins, and designed to be carried in a pocket or a ladies' purse.

300047600.label: statues
300047600.scope: Sculpture in the round, usually but not always depicting humans, animals, mythical beings, or small figure groups. Statues are relatively large in scale, being life-size, larger than life-size, or only slightly smaller than life-size. For small-scale representations of humans, animals, or mythical beings, use "figurines," "statuettes," or another appropriate term. For depictions of humans, animals, or mythical beings in media other than sculpture, use "figures (representations)."

300048153.label: bast
300048153.scope: Strong, woody fibers obtained from the phloem tissues (from the bark, stems, and leaves) of many plants, used for textiles, rope, and paper. Such fibers are characterized by fineness and flexibility. They are derived from flax, hemp, ramie, jute, abaca, cantala, henequen, sisal, pineapple, mitsumata, gampi, kozo, and other plants. Strong, woody fibers obtained from the phloem tissues (from the bark, stems, and leaves) of many plants, used for textiles, rope, and paper. Such fibers are characterized by fineness and flexibility. They are derived from flax, hemp, ramie, jute, abaca, cantala, henequen, sisal, pineapple, mitsumata, gampi, kozo, and other plants.

300049015.label: straps (fasteners)
300049015.scope: Strips of flexible material, especially leather, used for fastening or holding things together. May have a buckle or other fastener attached. For strips that pass over the shoulder, use "shoulder straps (object components)."

300052565.label: gutters (building drainage components)
300052565.scope: Shallow channels positioned on a building for the purpose of collecting and diverting water from a roof.

300053015.label: fastening
300053015.scope: The action of attaching something firmly or securely to something else with a bond of any kind.

300053028.label: abrasive cleaning
300053028.scope: Cleaning method that removes soil, discolorations, or coatings through the action of certain materials which impact and abrade the surface under pressure.

300053049.label: dyeing
300053049.scope: Process of applying a coloring matter that is in a solution or fine dispersion so that at least some of the coloring matter is taken up by the substance.

300053944.label: tanning (hide processing)
300053944.scope: An irreversible process of treating hides or skins with tannins to produce leather. Distinct from "tawing" which is reversible by washing. For the simpler process of drying a pelt, use "skin curing."

300053946.label: metalworking
300053946.scope: The act or process of shaping things out of metal or of decorating with metal.

300054588.label: alchemy
300054588.scope: A form of chemistry and speculative philosophy practiced in the Middle Ages and the Renaissance and concerned principally with discovering methods for transmuting base metal into gold and with finding a universal solvent and an elixir of life.

300055645.label: length
300055645.scope: The dimension of a straight horizontal line extending from the left side to the right side of a horizontal form. Usage may overlap with "width."

300055649.label: volume (quantity or mass)
300055649.scope: The quantity or mass of an object or material that occupies space.

300065017.label: altar screens
300065017.scope: Screens that separate the altar area from the space behind it. Distinct from "reredoses," which relate visually to the altar and may form part of the inner side of an altar screen.

300065928.label: doornails
300065928.scope: Large-headed nails with which doors, window shutters, or other such wooden coverings are studded for strength, protection, or ornamentation. Such a nail was also sometimes placed under a door knocker, to receive the blow and make a sound. For ornamental nails used in large numbers and primarily for decoration, particularly in historical Spain and its colonies, use "chatônes."

300069657.label: games
300069657.scope: Forms of competitive play, usually involving an element of strategy, especially to interfere with an opponent's play; may or may not require physical skill.

300079037.label: faucets (finish hardware)
300079037.scope: Devices used to draw or regulate the flow of water from a pipe.

300080149.label: knobs (handles)
300080149.scope: Handles in the form of relatively small masses, usually rounded, and projecting from a surface or extremity.

300081382.label: calculators
300081382.scope: Devices, usually small, that perform calculations, requiring manual action for each individual operation.

300081535.label: birdbaths
300081535.scope: Basins or other receptacles filled with water and usually placed in gardens or on lawns for birds to drink from or bathe in.

300081820.label: plate saddle hangers
300081820.scope: Hangers for steel-to-steel or for wood, comprising parallel inverted-U-shaped metal wires or bands joined at the open ends by a flat plate or bar, intended to be suspended from a horizontal member and attached to a horizontal beam or ceiling slab.

300082981.label: ships
300082981.scope: Watercraft generally larger and more seaworthy than boats, usually propelled by sails or engines.

300111961.label: holy water stoups
300111961.scope: Basins or bowls containing holy water at the entrance of a church. The font may be of various forms, either built into the wall, standing on a pedestal, or as a bucket hanging from a fixture. Often richly decorated, they are typically used by worshippers to cross themselves upon entering and exiting the church. The holy water font evolved from the fountain for ablutions that was placed in the center of the atrium of the early Christian basilica, and is still placed there in Eastern rites. Before entering the church, worshippers washed their hands and feet in accordance with a rite derived from Judaism. When the atrium of the Christian basilica was reduced to the proportions of a narrow court or a simple porch, the fountain gave way to a smaller structure.

300123316.label: flaps
300123316.scope: Components which are broad, limber, or flat, usually hanging or working on a hinge.

300125933.label: cathedrae (bishop's chairs)
300125933.scope: Chairs or thrones of a bishop in his cathedral church, in which he presides at solemn functions. The form is based on the ancient Roman cathedra. Originally the bishop's cathedra stood in the center of the apse, flanked at a lower level on either side by the benches where the assisting priests sat.

300127475.label: cages (enclosures)
300127475.scope: Boxlike enclosures having openwork of bars, wires, or the like used to confine or protect its occupant, or to admit light or ventilation. Typically reserved for large or small enclosures of this type used for animals, or for freestanding barred enclosures for humans. For such rooms in prisons, particularly if the room is enclosed within walls and having only a limited area of bars, prefer "prison cells."

300132254.label: vases
300132254.scope: Vessels of varying shape and size but which are usually taller than they are wide, varying greatly in actual form and use. For example, may refer to vessels for displaying flowers, or to ancient ceramic or metal vessel in a range of shapes and used to hold liquids, grain, or another substance.

300132399.label: flowers (plant components)
300132399.scope: The reproductive portions of any plant in the division Angiospermae, flowering plants. As popularly used, the term "flower" especially applies when part or all of the reproductive structure is distinctive in color and form.

300132406.label: vines
300132406.scope: Trailing or twining plants, whose stems require support.

300132407.label: shrubs
300132407.scope: Low-growing, woody perennials characterized by several branches at the base and by a lack of conspicuous trunks; generally restricted to plants under 6 m high.

300132436.label: herbs
300132436.scope: Nonwoody plants (perennials, biennials, or annuals) which produce seeds, but die down at the end of the growing season.

300132861.label: lace (needlework)
300132861.scope: Refers to a fine, openwork ornamental textile work formed by looping, interlacing, twisting, plaiting, or braiding threads of linen, cotton, silk, hair, metal, or another fiber to form designs or patterns. Lace may be made with a needle or with bobbins. Embroidery may be added. Modern lace may be made by machine. Openwork fabrics made on a loom and ornamental openwork knitting are generally not classified as lace. Lace is often white or monochromatic. True lace developed in the fourteenth century in Europe and the Middle East, although ornamented openwork fabrics were known in ancient cultures, including the Egyptian culture. Lace may be used as a border, edging, or insert on linens or apparel; it is also formed into large pieces of cloth used for hangings, draperies, apparel, or other items.

300132868.label: baize
300132868.scope: Loosely woven wool or cotton tabby, finished with a long nap to imitate felt and dyed in solid colors. Used as a protective covering for furnishings, as well as for costume, especially the lining of outerwear.

300132872.label: calico
300132872.scope: Cotton textile, heavier than muslin, plain, dyed, or with patterns printed in one or more colors. In the 18th and 19th centuries, the term referred to printed, colored or plain cloth from India; now it refers generally to cotton prints with small, stylized patterns.

300132886.label: flannel
300132886.scope: Soft twill with a slightly napped surface, made in various weights of wool or soft cotton yarn, often in combination with synthetic yarn.

300132887.label: fustian
300132887.scope: Strong cloth woven in a variety of patterns, in common use for bedding and lining for clothing from the 17th to the 19th century. Prior to the 17th century it was made of worsted, then pure cotton or mixes of cotton and linen became common; today generally a cotton twill with a short nap.

300132902.label: satin
300132902.scope: Woven textile characterized by a basic binding system or weave with smooth, shiny surface formed by long warp floats. Generally, each warp end passes over four or more adjacent weft picks and under the next one.

300133146.label: sets (groups)
300133146.scope: Assemblies of items that the creator intended to be kept or seen together, cuch as a tea set, a desk set, or a pair of terrestrial and celestial globes. A set differs from a collection in that it is typically smaller and it was intended by the creator to be grouped together. It is useful to catalog the set as a whole when the items in the set will not be cataloged separately or when there are characteristics of the whole set that may not be apparent in the individual records for the parts.

300133711.label: velvet (fabric weave)
300133711.scope: Warp pile weave, typically silk, with a short, soft dense pile produced by a supplementary warp that is raised in loops above the surface of the textile through the introduction of rods during the weaving; the loops may be cut or left uncut.

300133732.label: precious stone (material)
300133732.scope: Gemstone that is considered more valuable than other types, especially diamond, sapphire, emerald, ruby, and sometimes pearl.

300133746.label: padlocks
300133746.scope: Removable locks with a shackle that can be passed through a staple or link and then secured.

300133748.label: tin (metal)
300133748.scope: Pure metallic element having symbol Sn and atomic number 50; a soft, pliable, silvery white metal. Use also for this metal as processed and formed, usually in combination with other substances, to make various objects and materials.

300133751.label: steel (alloy)
300133751.scope: Any of various hard, strong, durable, malleable alloys of iron and carbon, often with other elements such as manganese, chromium, nickel, molybdenum, copper, tungsten, cobalt, or silicon; widely used as a structural material.

300136024.label: gameboards (board game elements)
300136024.scope: Flat boards or boardlike game accessories marked such that the progress of play can be tracked.

300137730.label: scoria
300137730.scope: The refuse, dross, or slag left after melting or smelting metal.

300140803.label: earthenware
300140803.scope: Pottery with a porous body, fired below 1200 degrees Centigrade. It is not vitrified, and must be glazed to render it nonporous.

300142324.label: canopies (bed components)
300142324.scope: Rooflike components suspended over the head of a bed by means of a cord attached to the ceiling; usually a cone-shaped or domed bowl with a valance all around, and with two or three curtains long enough to reach and encompass the foot of the bed. Use "testers" for rooflike components supported above the bed by posts.

300148821.label: gloves
300148821.scope: Coverings for the hand enclosing each finger separately, sometimes extending over the wrist and arm.

300160106.label: foil (metal by form)
300160106.scope: Thin sheet metal used chiefly for wrapping, insulation, electrical applications, and as an ornamental surface treatment. For extremely thin sheet metal used exclusively for applied decoration, use "leaf (metal)."

300161528.label: pocket knife
300161528.scope: Knives the blades of which fold into the handle to enable it to fit into a pocket.

300161848.label: andirons
300161848.scope: Devices, usually metal, comprising vertical elements and often a horizontal bar, supported by legs, and used to support logs in a fireplace. May be used with a "fireplace grate."

300162111.label: hand tools
300162111.scope: Any tools which are operated by and guided by hand.

300162391.label: cloth
300162391.scope: Generally, textile that is woven, felted, knit, pounded, or otherwise made into a flat piece. For textile in the form of continuous strands made from filaments of fiber by reeling, spinning, twisting, or throwing, see "yarn."

300162474.label: pasteboard (paper)
300162474.scope: A thick paper formed from multiple sheets adhered with an adhesive then pressed to produce a hard, stiff board. Pasteboard was used for book boards and playing cards in Europe from the early 16th to the late 18th centuries. It is now primarily used for making boxes and cartons.

300163224.label: textile working equipment
300163224.scope: General term for the tools, equipment, and supplies used to facilitate the preparation of materials made from fibers and woven fabrics.

300163295.label: damask
300163295.scope: Woven figured textile with one warp and one weft in which the pattern is formed by a contrast of binding systems, and appears on the face and the back in reverse positions.

300165849.label: supports (furniture components)
300165849.scope: Components that perform the action holding up or bearing the weight of something.

300168481.label: pincer tongs
300168481.scope: Iron tongs used for a variety of purposes, but usually used to hold heavy, round metal objects while they are being forged.

300170801.label: lecterns
300170801.scope: Elevated stands with a sloping top and usually a ledge at the bottom of the slope designed to support a book or script in a convenient position for a reader standing before it. A lectern may be placed on a table or mounted on a pedestal. A lectern In a church is usually situated in the chancel, sometimes inside a rood screen or tribune.

300174746.label: suitcase beds
300174746.scope: Portable, lightweight beds or cots that can be folded for transport and carried with handles, resembling a suitcase. The beds may include attached light bedding, or may be only the bedframe.

300175460.label: bedframes
300175460.scope: Frames of a bed, including bedrails, headboard, and footboard.

300178228.label: diptychs
300178228.scope: Works comprising pairs of panels hinged together. They were used by the ancient Romans for writing tablets, often having images on the outer surfaces. In Medieval and later times, they were used primarily to support images for altarpieces and other purposes, most often composed of carved ivory or of painted wood panels, with the primary images on the interior surfaces.

300178241.label: devotional images (religious works)
300178241.scope: Images, either two-dimensional pictures or three-dimensional, used in private piety or other religious purposes in a place of worship or home, intended as recipients of prayer or aids to meditation; distinct from images that serve the liturgy or are primarily didactic.

300178567.label: harquebuses
300178567.scope: Use generally for various types of light portable firearms used in Europe from the 14th to the early 17th century, fitted with a stock which allowed them to be held against the cheek, chest, or shoulder. The first models had a hooklike projection on the underside of the barrel to absorb recoil, and were rested upon a surface when fired.

300181108.label: wicks
300181108.scope: Those elements in lighting devices, usually cords, ribbons, or tubes of loosely woven, twisted, or braided fibers, that draw fuel to the flame by capillary action.

300181446.label: candle snuffers
300181446.scope: Devices for trimming the wicks of candles and lamps to keep the end of the wick even and clean; usually in the form of scissors with one blade bearing a boxlike receptacle to catch the cut-off ends of the charred wick. For scissorlike devices with flat disc-shaped ends used for pinching out a candle flame, use "douters." For cone-shaped devices used to extinguish flames, use "extinguishers."

300182830.label: tallow
300182830.scope: A hard fat obtained from animals, especially sheep, goats, and cattle, containing the fatty acids oleic acid, palmitic acid, stearic acid, linoleic acid, and myristic acid. Tallow is used in leather dressing and in the manufacture of soaps, lubricants, candles, and food.

300183060.label: bombards (cannons)
300183060.scope: Early cannons in use from the 14th to the 16th century, typically of large bore, made of wrought iron or cast bronze and firing stone cannonballs.

300183621.label: alum
300183621.scope: Colorless-to-white crystalline potassium aluminum sulfate; has a wide range of uses, including in treatment of leather and textile, in sizing paper, as a mordant in dyeing, and as a water-purifying agent.

300183627.label: salt (inorganic material)
300183627.scope: Any substance resulting from the combination of negative ions from acids and usually metal ions. For common table salt, or NaCl, use "sodium chloride."

300183670.label: cotton (fiber)
300183670.scope: White-to-yellowish seed-hair fibers of several species of the genus Gossypium, native to most subtropical areas of the world; used especially for making textile, cord, padding, rag paper, and for cellulose used for plastic and rayon.

300183798.label: trimming (decorative material)
300183798.scope: Collectively used for decorative or additional material serving to finish, decorate, or complete.

300183873.label: potash
300183873.scope: A potassium carbonate in the form of a white alkaline granular powder. It is used in glass manufacture, soft soap, and wool washing.

300183888.label: sodium chloride
300183888.scope: A crystalline compound, NaCl, found as colorless, cubic crystals that naturally occur in ocean water at concentrations of 2.6% and in the mineral halite. Sodium chloride is widely used for flavoring and preservation of food, for curing hides and skins, in electrochemical reactions and mordanting, in the precipitation of photographic emulsions, and for many other purposes. For any substance resulting from the combination of negative ions from acids and usually metal ions, use "salt (inorganic material)."

300183931.label: sugar
300183931.scope: A sweet crystalline carbohydrate, white when pure, obtained from a great variety of plant juices, but chiefly from those of the sugar-cane and sugar-beet, and forming an important article of human food.

300185256.label: millstones (equipment components)
300185256.scope: A pair of circular stones used for grinding grain or other substances, which are typically fed through a central hole in the upper stone.

300185311.label: irons (tools)
300185311.scope: Heatable devices usually with a flat metal base of some weight that are used to smooth, finish, or press cloth.

300185694.label: sails
300185694.scope: Sheets or panels of material, designed to catch the wind and convert its energy, as to propel a sailing vessel or drive a windmill.

300185756.label: carpets
300185756.scope: Rugs of some size whose primary use is to cover a flat surface; carpets constitute the largest and most familiar group of rugs.

300186112.label: mats (floor coverings)
300186112.scope: Protective floor coverings, such as those made of a coarse material intended to protect the floor, or those made as a resilient or padded covering to protect athletes during practice or performance.

300191086.label: visual works (works)
300191086.scope: Works of art, architecture, and any objects that occupy space, are perceived by the sense of sight, and are created or arranged, rather than naturally occurring. Of special interest are those objects conveying a symbolic or expressive meaning or an aesthetic experience, although visual works are not limited only to such works. Visual works generally exclude the intangible, however, designs for works never constructed may be included. Visual works include pictorial and sculptural works, as well as time-based works such as performance art. They also include utilitarian or ceremonial objects of the type collected or valued by museums, cultures, or individuals. Visual works do not include the performing arts.

300191094.label: strings (chordophone components)
300191094.scope: Lengths of any material that can produce a musical sound when held stretched and then plucked, bowed, struck, or otherwise excited. Common materials used are gut, silk, wire, nylon, palm fiber, and plastic.

300191621.label: honey
300191621.scope: Sweet viscous fluid produced by bees from the nectar collected from flowers.

300192952.label: sinew (material)
300192952.scope: In the context of materials, material comprising a tendon taken out of an animal body and used for some purpose, especially as a cord or thread, as a string in a musical instrument, or for another purpose.

300193015.label: vessels (containers)
300193015.scope: Containers designed to serve as receptacles for a liquid or other substance, usually those of circular section and made of some durable material; especially containers of this nature in domestic use, employed in connection with the preparation or serving of food or drink, and usually of a size suitable for carrying by hand.

300193293.label: rawhide
300193293.scope: Untanned skin or hide which has had the flesh and hair removed and allowed to dry into a desired shape.

300193371.label: pelt (animal material)
300193371.scope: Material comprising the hide or skin of an animal, usually a mammal, with the hair or wool left on.

300193374.label: sheepskin
300193374.scope: The skin of a sheep, with or without wool left on, prepared for any of various uses such as in garments, as leather or as parchment. The leather made from sheepskin is soft with little grain, and is not particularly durable.

300194222.label: pages (components)
300194222.scope: Individual sides of a leaf, recto or verso; the individual sides of leaves resulting from folding a sheet, as of paper or parchment, whether blank or containing writing, printing, or other matter. Distinguished from a "folio" in that a folio is numbered on only the front side.

300194498.label: baskets (containers)
300194498.scope: Containers made of twigs, rushes, thin strips of wood, or other flexible material woven together.

300194509.label: bags (generic containers)
300194509.scope: Containers or receptacles of leather, cloth, paper, or other flexible material, often capable of being closed at the mouth. For ladies' bags intended to carry personal articles, use "bags (costume accessories)." For large containers of cloth or plastic for carrying, transporting, or storing produce and other items, use "sacks."

300194514.label: barrels (containers)
300194514.scope: Cylindrical containers, usually wooden, with slightly bulging sides made of staves hooped together, and with flat, parallel ends.

300194515.label: casks
300194515.scope: Barrel-shaped containers, especially those stronger and larger than barrels, made of staves, headings, and hoops usually closely fitted together so as to hold liquids.

300194541.label: vats (containers)
300194541.scope: Large containers used for holding or storing liquids.

300194553.label: pouches
300194553.scope: Small or moderate size bags for carrying small articles, often having drawstrings, a flap, or closure hardware.

300194600.label: bullion
300194600.scope: Gold or silver considered in mass rather than in value, often in ingot or bar form.

300195311.label: tubs (containers)
300195311.scope: Wide, low containers originally made of wooden staves held together by hoops and sometimes having a lid or wire handles or both. Also, similar containers made of metal or plastic.

300195322.label: canisters
300195322.scope: Cylindrical or rectangular containers usually of lightweight metal, plastic, or laminated pasteboard used for holding dry products.

300195347.label: jars
300195347.scope: Deep, wide-mouthed vessels used for holding a variety of substances, usually without handles and generally cylindrical, although sometimes made in other shapes. For narrower-necked vessels, use "bottles."

300195349.label: kettles (vessels)
300195349.scope: Vessels, commonly of metal, for boiling water or other liquids over a fire or other source of heat; includes covered metal vessels with a spout, used to boil water for domestic purposes.

300195535.label: saucers (plates)
300195535.scope: Small plates of concave form, usually circular, either for eating food or as a stand for a cup. Generally, those for use with a cup have a slight depression in the center in which to place the cup.

300195678.label: flags
300195678.scope: Pieces of cloth or other flexible material, usually attached along one side to a pole or cord, intended for such purposes as symbolizing a nation or organization, or as a means of signaling.

300195679.label: banners
300195679.scope: Pieces of cloth or other flexible material painted with signs or decorative designs and intended to be displayed by hanging or suspending. In heraldry, refers to square flags bearing heraldic devices. For other cloths intended to symbolize or to signal, use "flags."

300195708.label: weighing devices
300195708.scope: Instruments, machines, or other apparatus used for determining weight, which is the amount of force exerted on an object or substance by gravity or the amount of force needed to support it.

300195805.label: balances (scales)
300195805.scope: Scales with a horizontal bar pivoting about a central fulcrum, creating equal-length arms; suspended from the ends of the arms are pans or baskets, in one of which is placed the item being weighed and in the other, a premeasured weight.

300195960.label: chiming clocks
300195960.scope: Clocks that audibly mark periods of time by striking or playing musical notes.

300196293.label: scales (weighing devices)
300196293.scope: Instruments for determining the weight of objects or substances.

300196395.label: cauldrons
300196395.scope: Large, open vessels, especially those used over an open fire.

300196416.label: chafing dishes
300196416.scope: Dishes supplied with a heat source (such as a fuel lamp or candle) used for cooking or keeping food warm. The term is sometimes applied to vessels containing charcoal or other fuel and upon which another container with food may be placed.

300196517.label: dripping pans
300196517.scope: Shallow metal pans used under roasting meats to catch the drippings.

300196566.label: hogsheads
300196566.scope: Large casks or barrels; especially ones of a capacity between 63 and 140 gallons.

300196577.label: gallipots (vessels)
300196577.scope: Small, usually ceramic vessels with narrow mouths, especially ones used by apothecaries to hold medicines.

300196691.label: mazers
300196691.scope: Drinking vessels in the form of a wide, flat-bottomed, shallow bowl; originally of wood (especially maple) and often having silver or gilt mounts. Many have a central ornamental print on the interior.

300196797.label: inkwells
300196797.scope: Small vessels for holding ink into which a pen can be dipped. For bottles in which ink is sold, see "ink bottles."

300197059.label: armor components
300197059.scope: Armor pieces which are physical parts of or are affixed to other pieces and cannot function alone. For individual armor pieces which can be worn and function individually or in sets, see "armor."

300197197.label: containers (receptacles)
300197197.scope: Receptacles or formed or flexible coverings designed to hold, store, or ship objects or substances.

300197224.label: spouts (container components)
300197224.scope: Tubular protruberances through which the contents of a vessel may be poured or sometimes drunk.

300197240.label: spigots
300197240.scope: A type of valve or cock used to control the flow of liquid through a tap, as found on coffee urns, tea urns, wine fountains, and the like.

300197291.label: hampers
300197291.scope: Large baskets, usually having a cover or lid, for packing, storing, or transporting food, laundry, or other articles.

300197296.label: packing boxes
300197296.scope: Boxes intended primarily for packing goods for transport or storage.

300197367.label: blankets (coverings)
300197367.scope: Large rectangular coverings of thick but soft material, used especially for warmth.

300197555.label: weights (scale components)
300197555.scope: Objects of known mass for use on scales during weighing.

300197647.label: dials
300197647.scope: Plates, disks, faces, or other surfaces with markings or figures for indicating such information as time, measurement, or frequency, usually by means of pointing devices.

300197954.label: coverlets
300197954.scope: Woven bedcovers, especially those made of a single piece of fabric, usually of wool and cotton.

300197990.label: quilts
300197990.scope: Bedcovers consisting of three layers (top, backing, and filling) joined by quilting, which is stitching that typically forms decorative patterns or designs. The term is also used loosely to refer to similar bedcovers joined by other means. Quilts are distinguished from "comforters," which are warmer, heavily wadded bedcovers on which the design of the stitching is not as elaborate or decorative. In addition to serving as bedcovers, quilts may also be used as wall hangings or for another purpose.

300198452.label: braziers (cooking, heating equipment)
