300198452.scope: Receptacles, usually metal or terracotta, having a base designed to hold live coals, and sometimes with a grate or pierced top, used for heating a room or for heating or cooking food.

300198626.label: hourglasses
300198626.scope: Sandglasses for which one hour is required for the given quantity to fall from the upper to the lower vessel.

300198675.label: latten
300198675.scope: Copper-zinc-tin alloy, sometimes also including lead, made by melting ground calamine ore with charcoal and copper; used in the Medieval period for weights and utensils.

300198733.label: sheaths (cases)
300198733.scope: Cases or coverings for the blade of a sword, dagger, or other instrument to which it fits closely.

300198822.label: vials
300198822.scope: Small or moderate-sized vessels mainly for medicinal and toilet preparations.

300198893.label: chamber pots
300198893.scope: Portable bowls kept in a bedroom and used for the discharge of urine, excrement, etc., especially at night. Usually having shaped convex sides, a flat bottom, and a single loop or scroll handle; some have covers.

300199785.label: cooking utensils
300199785.scope: Instruments used when preparing and cooking food.

300200095.label: ladles
300200095.scope: Spoonlike utensils with a deep bowl and a relatively long handle used for lifting, conveying, or serving cream, soup, punch, or other liquids.

300200162.label: wafer irons
300200162.scope: Long-handled pair of iron palette tongs for baking wafers, often having a bed with a molded or engraved design that is impressed on the wafer batter in baking.

300200179.label: pepper mills
300200179.scope: Small hand-held devices for storing and grinding peppercorns.

300200181.label: querns
300200181.scope: Simple, hand-operated mills consisting of two circular stones; used to grind grain.

300200533.label: nutcrackers
300200533.scope: Instruments or devices for cracking the shells of nuts.

300200832.label: griddles
300200832.scope: Flat, heated surfaces, especially on top of stoves, for cooking food.

300201088.label: sieves
300201088.scope: Meshed or perforated devices or utensils through which dry loose material (as flour) is winnowed or refined, material containing liquid is strained, or soft solids (as hard-boiled eggs) are comminuted by forcing (as with a pestle).

300201090.label: graters
300201090.scope: Any of various tools for grating, powdering or shredding food or other materials handled in a similar way, such as pressed blocks of tobacco or cosmetics.

300201151.label: spits (cooking and heating devices)
300201151.scope: Pointed rods for thrusting through and holding meat and other foods while cooking before or over a source of heat; sometimes made as a component part of rotisseries and other cooking and heating devices. Use "skewers" for long pinlike utensils used to hold small pieces of food while cooking or dipping.

300201267.label: sackbuts
300201267.scope: Early English version of the trombone, in use from Medieval times up to the 18th century.

300201648.label: war hammers
300201648.scope: Use specifically for European percussive weapons having a heavy head, typically with a blunt or cusped face and at least one blade or spike at the back of the head or on top of the staff, various forms of which were in use from the 13th to the 17th century. Also used very generally for hammers used as fighting weapons in nearly all parts of the world since the Stone Age.

300201776.label: hauberks
300201776.scope: Long shirts of mail protecting the arms, torso, and legs to mid-thigh, sometimes also covering the head. They were common in Europe from the 11th to the 14th century.

300201780.label: legharnesses
300201780.scope: Sets of armor for the leg.

300201964.label: gemstone
300201964.scope: Precious or semiprecious stone that can be cut, polished, or otherwise dressed for use as gems; distinguished from "gems," which are made of gemstone that has been worked or other material such as pearl.

300202510.label: alphabet books
300202510.scope: Books designed to display the letters of the alphabet, often with accompanying illustrations; may be used to teach the alphabet or as vehicles for an illustrator's art.

300202819.label: boards (binding components)
300202819.scope: Stiff upper and lower covers of books comprising stiff, thick cardboard or other material, often covered with leather, cloth or another material.

300203437.label: closures (container components)
300203437.scope: Object components which are used to cover or close a mouth or other openings on containers.

300203447.label: bungs
300203447.scope: Stoppers for the openings of casks where they are filled.

300203596.label: bowls (vessels)
300203596.scope: Rounded vessels that are generally wider than they are high, usually hemispherical or nearly so. A bowl may have a spreading base or foot ring and sometimes two handles or a cover. Distinguished from a cup, which is rather deep than wide.

300203658.label: gridirons (culinary tools)
300203658.scope: Frames of parallel metal bars used for broiling food over coals or an open fire.  Also, wood gratings or racks for the same purpose.

300203708.label: gorget plates
300203708.scope: Components of some close helmets and closed burgonets, protecting the neck, consisting of two or three articulated metal lames riveted at the front to the bevor and at the rear to the skull. They also form the lower part of the falling buffe for a burgonet.

300203712.label: skulls (helmet components)
300203712.scope: Helmet components, constituting that part which directly covers and protects the cranium; they occur in various shapes and may be made from either a single piece of metal or two overlapping halves joined at the comb.

300203727.label: projectile weapons
300203727.scope: Weapons that launch projectiles toward targets.

300203988.label: stocks (firearm components)
300203988.scope: The combinations of frame and handle that contain or join together the various other components of a firearm so that it can be handled, aimed, and fired.

300204122.label: bed hangings
300204122.scope: Curtains and other cloth hangings on or around a bed; used for decoration, privacy, control of light and drafts, or as protective coverings.

300204482.label: boar spears
300204482.scope: Spears designed for hunting wild boars and other large game, having a transverse bar fitted below the broad blade.

300204516.label: hangers (swords)
300204516.scope: Swords with relatively short, pointed, single-edged, curved or straight blades designed primarily for cutting. They served as all-purpose weapons, used by civilians, hunters, sailors, and infantry soldiers, from the 16th to the 19th century.

300204598.label: sheets (bed coverings)
300204598.scope: Bed coverings of cotton, linen, or the like, commonly used in pairs so that one is immediately above and the other immediately below the sleeper.

300204665.label: powder flasks
300204665.scope: Portable containers of wood, horn, metal, leather, or ceramic used to hold the priming powder or gunpowder for firearms. They normally terminated in a metal nozzle which also served as a powder measure, closed by a plug or spring cap, and are often highly decorated. Prefer "powder horns" for those made from the horn of a cow or oxen.

300204798.label: galoshes
300204798.scope: Overshoes of rubber or other waterproof fabric, especially those that extend above the ankle and that often have buckles or other fasteners. Use "rubbers" for overshoes without buckles or fasteners that are cut below the ankle.

300204864.label: altar cloths
300204864.scope: Cloth coverings for altars often with decorative edgings and individual embroidered motifs.

300204880.label: tabernacle veils
300204880.scope: Textile coverings for the tabernacle, which holds the consecrated host and is located in, on, or near the high altar of a church. The tabernacle veil is often of a prescribed liturgical color, based on the period of the church calendar.

300204905.label: upholstery
300204905.scope: Refers to the fixed soft coverings for furniture, especially seating and reclining furniture. Originally referred to all the textile components of a room supplied by upholsterers, including wall hangings, bed hangings, window curtains, and table coverings.

300204911.label: springs (elastic objects)
300204911.scope: Elastic bodies, often strips or wires of steel coiled spirally, that recover their shape after being compressed, bent, or stretched.

300204952.label: bed coverings
300204952.scope: Term generally applied to any textile used to cover a bed.

300204962.label: table carpets
300204962.scope: Heavy table covers of knotted pile, tapestry or needlework.

300204969.label: tablecloths
300204969.scope: Cloths for covering the top of a table, especially during a meal.

300204985.label: pillowcases
300204985.scope: Sacklike removable and washable coverings for pillows, often matching bolster cases and sheets.  For decorative coverings enclosing or laid over pillows use "pillow shams."

300205002.label: tapestries
300205002.scope: Heavy, woven textiles used as wall hangings, curtains, upholstery, or to hang from windows or balconies. Tapestries are characterized by decoration that may include ornamental or pictorial subjects; they often have details that are painted or embroidered. They are usually of wool and hand-woven on a tapestry loom by a process that differs from cloth-weaving in that the weft travels only to the warp at the edge of a particular color or pattern in the design, rather traveling from edge to edge of the entire piece of fabric. Various techniques are used in mixing and overlaying colors to create shading and patterns. The term also refers to machine-woven imitations of hand-made hangings.

300205010.label: hangings (coverings)
300205010.scope: Artifacts, usually flexible, often textiles, that are hung to cover or conceal interior spaces, surfaces, or furnishings, especially for protection, warmth, or embellishment.

300206700.label: tuns (casks)
300206700.scope: Large casks for holding liquids, especially wine, ale, or beer.

300207024.label: corslets (half armor)
300207024.scope: Light half armor worn by heavy infantry from the early 16th to the mid-17th century in Europe, at first comprised of a gorget, spaudlers, breastplate, backplate, tassets, vambraces, gauntlets, and an open helmet, but no legharness. In the 17th century, arm defenses were usually omitted.

300207740.label: milk strainers
300207740.scope: Pierced bowl-like strainers or specially designed pails used to strain milk.

300207796.label: bakestones
300207796.scope: Flat pieces of stone, ceramic materials, or iron used for baking.

300208335.label: fonts (type composition equipment)
300208335.scope: Historically, a collection of type consisting of all letters, numerals, punctuation marks, and other symbols belonging to a single design and point size, and not including other sets of characters such as the bold type of the same design family. In photocomposition and desktop publishing, a font is the set of characters and other symbols of one style available as a unit, such as through a strip of film or a program module.

300209829.label: doublets
300209829.scope: Close-fitting waist-length or hip-length garments with or without sleeves worn by men from the 15th to the 17th century and for similar garments reinforced by mail and worn under armor. Also refers to sleeved, hip-length garments worn as part of military uniforms by the Scottish units of the British army after 1855.

300209852.label: robes (main garments)
300209852.scope: Long, loose garments that tend to be of one piece and to open down the front. Examples include ordinary wear for men and women, dating from the Middle Ages forward in the West and common yet today in Asian and African countries; and similar garments often of elegant style worn for ceremonial or official occasions or as a symbol of office or profession. For women’s dresses, use "gowns." For loose-fitting garments, often wraparound and worn to the bath or informally around the house use "bathrobes."

300209869.label: tunics
300209869.scope: Simple slip-on garments made with or without sleeves and usually knee-length or longer and belted at the waist; especially those worn by men and women of ancient Greece and Rome. Also, garments extending from the neckline to the waist or longer, usually high-necked and worn over other garments.

300209887.label: jerkins (jackets)
300209887.scope: Close-fitting, hip-length jackets without sleeves, usually collarless and secured with a belt, especially those worn over a doublet during the 16th and 17th centuries. Use also for similar garments with closures made of woven or knitted cloth or leather and worn during the 20th century as protective outerwear or to carry equipment by military personnel.

300209890.label: mantelets
300209890.scope: Very short mantles, often trimmed with lace or fringe.

300209904.label: vests (garments)
300209904.scope: Close-fitting main garments extending to the waist or just below. Sleeveless and usually collarless, and often having buttons or pockets. For close-fitting main garments extending below the waistline that are usually front-buttoning and may have sleeves, that are worn over a shirt and under a coat or jacket, use "waistcoats."

300209935.label: trousers
300209935.scope: Exposed bifurcated garments which extend from waist or hips to the ankle or sometimes to the knee or just below.

300209947.label: dressing gowns
300209947.scope: Men's or women's loose, informal garments, often coat-like, worn when partly or fully undressed. Generally warm and often full-length; may be worn with a rope belt.

300209970.label: fans (equipment)
300209970.scope: Devices used for producing or moving large volumes of air or gas with a low compression ratio; usually consisting of a rotating paddle wheel or airscrew.

300210002.label: belts (costume accessories)
300210002.scope: Flexible straps or bands generally encircling the waist or hips or passing over the shoulder and usually having some type of fastener, such as a buckle; worn for decoration, support, or to carry such items as weapons, tools, or money.

300210012.label: mittens (handwear)
300210012.scope: Coverings for the hand enclosing four fingers in one section and the thumb in another section.

300210027.label: gaiters
300210027.scope: Coverings of cloth, leather, or similar material worn over the ankle and sometimes lower leg.

300210042.label: pattens (overshoes)
300210042.scope: Overshoes consisting of a sole, usually set on bands of iron, often ring-shaped, and fastened over footwear by tie straps, worn to elevate the foot for protection from mud, dirt, or wetness. For footwear with a thick sole usually of wood, but sometimes of leather or cork, use "clogs."

300210058.label: collars (neckwear)
300210058.scope: Shaped articles worn at the neckline of a garment, either separate or attached.

300210312.label: fuller's earth
300210312.scope: Clay possessing a high absorptive capacity; it is extensively used as an absorbent in refining and decolorizing oil and fat.

300210423.label: cassocks (liturgical costume)
300210423.scope: Ankle-length garments of various types, but usually having long, narrow sleeves; worn especially members of the clergy and others participating in church services.

300210424.label: chasubles (liturgical vestments)
300210424.scope: Sleeveless outer vestments in the form of a wide cloak or mantle that slips over the wearer's head and remains open at the sides. Chasubles are worn over the alb and stole by the celebrant at Mass.

300210429.label: copes
300210429.scope: Long, semi-circular cloaklike garments fastened at the neck with a morse; worn by ecclesiastics in processions and on other ceremonial occasions. Also, similar garments worn as coronation or processional robes by laymen.

300210450.label: vestments (ecclesiastical costume)
300210450.scope: Garments worn by priests or other ecclesiastics during divine service, such as performing mass or other rituals, as appropriate to the rite and indicative of their hierarchical rank.

300210524.label: shoelaces
300210524.scope: Laces or strings used for fastening shoes.

300210530.label: sleeves (costume)
300210530.scope: Shaped coverings for the arm. Originally made separate from the main garment and attached by lacing through eyelets at the shoulder; later, often made as component parts of garments.

300210573.label: undershirt
300210573.scope: Shirts, with or without sleeves, worn next to the body and under another shirt. Usually pullovers of a cotton jersey. For similar garments worn as main garments use "T-shirts."

300210585.label: girdles (underwear)
300210585.scope: Women's underwear, often partly or entirely of elastic or boned, for supporting and shaping the appearance of the abdomen, hips, and buttocks.

300210605.label: swaddling clothes
300210605.scope: Term for clothes worn by infants that restrict movement to some extent, including either clothing consisting of narrow strips of cloth used to swaddle an infant or an infant's long clothes.

300210720.label: bonnets (hats)
300210720.scope: Soft hats usually tied under the chin and having a front brim; formerly worn by women, but now mostly children.

300210736.label: cornets (headdresses)
300210736.scope: Term applied to women's headdresses which vary in style from the 14th to the 18th century, but which are often of conical shape and usually made of delicate materials with lappets of lace or ribbon.

300210977.label: bolts (arrows)
300210977.scope: Short, thick arrows fitted with flights and a head of any of various shapes, often square or blunt, designed to be shot by crossbows.

300211037.label: toys (recreational artifacts)
300211037.scope: Material objects contrived for amusement rather than for practical use by children or pets, or intended as collectibles by adults. Toys are generally miniature versions of real beings or objects that lend themselves to imaginative or imitative play. Toys may also be items for use in games. Among the earliest toys were dolls and balls.

300211065.label: balance beams
300211065.scope: Narrow, and relatively long, wooden or steel beams set horizontally several feet above the floor and upon which performers demonstrate balancing acts and gymnastic moves.

300211084.label: dice
300211084.scope: Small polyhedral objects, usually cubes, that are marked on each face with dots, symbols, or numbers, used as game pieces, for casting lots, and for other purposes. An example is dice marked on each face distinctively with from one to six dots such that opposite faces add to seven; may also be used for similar cubes marked with other numbers or symbols specially created for gambling or certain other games.

300211087.label: dolls (figurines)
300211087.scope: Figurines representing humans or animals, including but not restricted to those intended as toys for children, usually girls, or as collectibles for adults. Dolls are commonly in the form of a baby or woman, often with changeable clothes; they may have moveable arms and legs. Doll may be made of cloth (rag dolls), wood, clay, porcelain, wax, paper, plastic, celluloid, corn husks, or other materials.  Dolls may also be figurines used for ceremonial, religious, or decorative purposes. Archaeological evidence suggests that dolls were the first playthings; they have been found in Babylonian and Egyptian tombs from ca. 3000 BCE. In ancient Greece and Rome, maturing girls consecrated their childhood dolls to the goddesses. Cloth dolls in the form of animals are generally called "stuffed toys."

300211101.label: game pieces (game elements)
300211101.scope: The objects, usually small and of hard durable materials, manipulated directly by participants during the play of card, table, and board games.

300211249.label: rackets (sports equipment)
300211249.scope: Batlike objects with long handles and oval or round heads containing tightly stretched netting for striking balls or shuttlecocks in various sports; for similar but smaller objects with solid heads for use in table tennis, use "paddles (ball game equipment)."

300211294.label: playing cards
300211294.scope: Cards made in sets of a designated number and marked for use as game accessories during play. The markings or designs may follow a standard suit or rank system or may be special and individualized.

300211432.label: chessmen
300211432.scope: The pieces used in the game of chess, in modern sets generally comprising kings, queens, bishops, knights, rooks, and pawns.

300212059.label: aglets
300212059.scope: Tags or ornaments at the ends of laces, ribbons, or points that tie garments or footwear. Also refers to any of various ornamental tags, studs, or plates worn on costume; may be at pendent end of a cord or similar object or sewn directly onto garments or headgear.

300212499.label: shirts (main garments)
300212499.scope: Generally refers to various types of main garments for the upper body, made with or without sleeves and worn over or tucked in the waistband of a skirt, trousers, or the like. Usually having a collar, which may be detachable, often a front opening, and sometimes pockets. Specifically often refers to an article of male attire with long sleeves terminating in wristbands or cuffs. It originally referred to undergarments for the upper part of the body, made of linen, calico, flannel, silk, or other washable material; originally always worn next to the skin.

300212695.label: carts
300212695.scope: Strong vehicles, having two or sometimes three wheels and without springs. Usually animal-drawn and built for utility purposes, used in farming operations, and for carrying heavy goods. Some varieties were designed as sporting vehicles or for personal transportation. For utility vehicles having four wheels, use "wagons."

300212971.label: harnesses
300212971.scope: The complete equipment by which draft animals are attached to vehicles of any kind; sometimes also used for riding accoutrements.

300212997.label: wimples (headcloths)
300212997.scope: Soft headcloths, especially of linen or silk, wrapped around the throat and passing under the chin from one side of the head to the other, and pinned to a band, hat or the hair. Of a type originating in the Medieval period and retained by nuns of various religions to the present day.

300213068.label: spars (watercraft components)
300213068.scope: Denotes any wooden support for the rigging of a vessel, including the booms, gaffs, masts, and yards.

300213077.label: oars
300213077.scope: Long slender shafts, usually wood, shaped to a round handle or grip at one end and flat-tipped blade at the other; for rowing. For similar but shorter devices with round-tipped blades for propelling small boats, use "paddles (watercraft equipment)."

300213129.label: potassium nitrate
300213129.scope: A transparent white crystalline compound of the composition KNO3, used in the production of explosives, pyrotechnics, matches, rocket propellants, and fertilizers.

300213343.label: mail (metal fabric)
300213343.scope: Metal fabric consisting of iron or steel rings, riveted or pressed together, typically used in armor.

300213346.label: lames (plates)
300213346.scope: Thin pieces or plates of any substance, but often of metal. Examples are the relatively pliable metal plates often used in making armor pieces.

300213433.label: coifs
300213433.scope: Close-fitting caps made in a variety of shapes and sizes and worn at various periods by men and women, sometimes surmounted by a hat or headdress.

300213699.label: arsenic
300213699.scope: A grayish-white element with symbol As and atomic number 33, having a metallic luster, vaporizing when heated, and forming poisonous compounds.

300213709.label: helmet visors
300213709.scope: Components of helmets that protect the eyes, the entire face, sometimes including the neck.

300213888.label: cauls (costume components)
300213888.scope: During the 18th and 19th centuries, term used to describe soft crowns found on bonnets or caps.

300214764.label: funeral palls
300214764.scope: Palls, usually of black, purple, or white velvet, used during the funeral ceremony to cover the coffin, hearse, or tomb. May be decorated with commemorative inscriptions or funerary portraits.

300215026.label: wrappers (containers)
300215026.scope: Textiles or other materials used as wrappings for parcels, gifts, or articles that need to be put away or carried from one place to another.

300215543.label: trunks (containers)
300215543.scope: Rigid, boxlike containers, usually large and often reinforced, for packing clothing and other personal gear or articles for travel or storage.

300215860.label: stomachers
300215860.scope: Stiff panels, usually triangular in shape and often heavily decorated, inserted in an open bodice to cover the corset.

300215863.label: cutting boards
300215863.scope: Boards often of wood and sometimes of plastic or other synthetic material, used as firm surfaces for cutting food.

300216024.label: colobia
300216024.scope: Half-sleeved or sleeveless tunics worn as ecclesiastical vestments before the 4th century.  Also, similar garments worn by monks and by kings as coronation robes.

300216035.label: points (fasteners)
300216035.scope: Ties or laces, as of leather or ribbon, finished with metal tabs or aglets at the ends. Originally used to fasten together parts of costume; later, tied in bows and used for trimming.

300216050.label: smocks (protective wear)
300216050.scope: Refers to loose garments, generally garments that cover the upper body, the term being derived from an old English word for shirt or chemise. It can refer to loose, outer garments designed to protect more valuable attire from soil or paint. It can also refer to loose undergarments, which were often gathered or embroidered at the neck and sleeves and were originally intended to protect more valuable outer garments from perspiration and other bodily soil and fluids.

300216053.label: waistcoats (garments)
300216053.scope: Close-fitting main garments extending to below the waistline. Usually front buttoning and sleeveless, but may have sleeves, especially garments from the 18th century. Worn over a shirt and under a coat or jacket. For close-fitting main garments extending to the waist or just below that are sleeveless and usually collarless, use "vests (garments)."

300216195.label: handkerchiefs
300216195.scope: Pieces of cloth, usually square, varying in size and material, carried for usefulness or as a costume accessory.

300216610.label: chessboards
300216610.scope: Gameboards of 64 squares arranged in eight vertical rows called files and eight horizontal rows called ranks. These squares alternate between two colors: one light, such as white or beige; and the other dark, such as black or green. The board is set between the two opponents so that each player has a light-colored square at the right-hand corner. Chessboards are identical to checkerboards except for the colors, which tend to be black and red in checkerboards.

300216616.label: table linens
300216616.scope: Linens used in setting a table for dining, such as tablecloths and napkins.

300216632.label: towels
300216632.scope: Rectangular pieces of cloth, paper, or other absorbent material, used for wiping or drying.

300216644.label: napkins (culinary textile)
300216644.scope: Relatively small pieces of cloth or paper used for wiping the mouth and hands and protecting clothes while dining.

300216691.label: table coverings
300216691.scope: Covers, often made of cloth, used over tables.

300216958.label: trivets
300216958.scope: Stands, supports, or flat devices, usually with long or short feet, often three, but sometimes with none and which may also have a handle, used to elevate a vessel in a hearth while cooking or to protect a surface, as of a table or counter, from being damaged by the heat of a hot object, such as a cooking vessel or flatiron.

300217875.label: balls (object genres)
300217875.scope: Round or roundish objects having the general shape of a sphere, which is a geometric shape comprising all points equidistant from the center. Balls may be of various materials and sizes, inflated, soft, or solid used in many different contexts and applications.

300217912.label: board games (game sets)
300217912.scope: Game sets for activities that involve the moving of game pieces across a gameboard.

300219429.label: anchors (watercraft equipment)
300219429.scope: Any of various devices dropped to the bottom of a body of water and designed to bury themselves there in order to restrict the movement of watercraft or other floating objects.

300220519.label: religious texts
300220519.scope: General term for texts of religion, sacred beliefs, or related to religious beliefs and practices.

300220741.label: girdles (belts)
300220741.scope: Narrow belts, cords, sashes or the like, usually decorative and worn at the waist to fasten or confine garments or as a means of carrying small objects such as purses or keys.

300220755.label: soap boxes (container for personal grooming)
300220755.scope: Small boxes or receptacles intended primarily for soap. Common examples made as spherical, perforated containers used to hold a ball of scented soap. May be part of a toilet set. For open containers used to hold a bar of soap, use "soap dishes."

300220822.label: pomanders
300220822.scope: Small containers for fragrant spices or perfumes originally intended to be carried to ward off infections. Perforated and usually globular, apple-shaped, or composed of fitted sections.

300220971.label: troughs (containers)
300220971.scope: Long, narrow, open receptacles, usually boxlike in shape. The term is used chiefly in the context of holding water or food for animals, but may be extended to any large tank or vat of similar shape used for other purposes.

300220999.label: washbowls
300220999.scope: Large bowls or basins for washing one's hands and face, usually accompanied by a pitcher.

300221157.label: crystal (material by form)
300221157.scope: A solid body having a characteristic internal structure and enclosed by systematically arranged plane surfaces.

300221387.label: volupers
300221387.scope: Type of ornamental headdress worn from the 14th to the 16th century, especially by women.

300222050.label: baby dolls (recreational dolls)
300222050.scope: Dolls whose expressions, proportions, and dress mimic those of infants.

300222748.label: chess
300222748.scope: Board game, held to be one of the oldest and most popular, played by two opponents on a checkered board with specially designed pieces of contrasting colors, commonly white and black. Players alternate turns in accordance with fixed rules, each player attempting to force the opponent's principal piece, the King, into checkmate, which is a position where it is unable to avoid capture. It first appeared in India in the 6th century CE; by the 10th century, it had spread from Asia to the Middle East and Europe. It remains popular and the focus of popular amateur and professional competitions.

300223016.label: sheet metal
300223016.scope: Metal rolled to any given thickness between 0.06 and 0.249 inches and cut into rectangular sections.

300223750.label: impurities
300223750.scope: Extraneous matter, especially of an inferior or contaminating nature, that is mixed with desirable matter.

300224238.label: hatbands
300224238.scope: Bands encircling the crown of a hat; sometimes worn as a badge of mourning.

300224239.label: livery (uniforms)
300224239.scope: Distinctive uniforms worn by servants or other classes of people.

300224858.label: upper cannons
300224858.scope: Tubular pieces of plate armor shaped to cover the upper arm, constituting part of the vambrace.

300225933.label: eyeglass cases
300225933.scope: Small cases of varying form and material intended primarily for holding eyeglasses. May be quite decorative and sometimes suspended from a chain so they can be worn on the person.

300227076.label: projectile weapon components
300227076.scope: Parts or components of projectile weapons.

300227408.label: balls (bullets)
300227408.scope: Solid bullets of spherical or conical shape, containing no propellant or explosive, fired from small arms. For the spherical projectiles made to be fired from cannons, use "cannonballs."

300227431.label: flails (weapons)
300227431.scope: Weapons consisting of a stout handle at the end of which are attached, by means of a chain, two or more iron-clad balls, a short iron-clad bar, or a wooden rod with iron spikes. They date back to at least the 13th century.

300227807.label: cord yarn
300227807.scope: Firm yarn produced by twisting together two or more single strands of yarn. For yarn produced by twisting together two or more plied strands of yarn, use "cabled yarn."

300227812.label: crewel wool
300227812.scope: Fine, loosely twisted, two-ply, worsted yarn used in embroidering.

300227830.label: fringe
300227830.scope: Trimming consisting of long or short lengths of straight or twisted thread, cord, or tassel; often grouped or knotted in various designs.

300227846.label: lining (material)
300227846.scope: Layer of material used to line the inner side or surface of something to reinforce or protect it.

300227874.label: pleats
300227874.scope: Folds of definite, even width, made in a material such as textile or paper by doubling it upon itself; usually stitched, sometimes pressed in place.

300227912.label: toweling
300227912.scope: Textile made for towels and similar items, woven by the yard; usually made of absorbent fiber, such as cotton or linen, and woven in narrow widths.

300227915.label: twill
300227915.scope: Refers to a woven textile characterized by parallel diagonal ridges or ribs, produced by passing the weft threads over one and under two or more threads of the warp, instead of over and under in regular succession, as in plain weaving. Regular twill features a diagonal line that is repeated regularly, usually running from the left to right at a 45-degree angle and upward. The weave may be varied in several ways, including changing the angle or direction of the twill line, as exemplified in herringbone twill.

300227943.label: worsted
300227943.scope: Smooth compact yarn spun with average to hard twist from long wool fibers that have been carded and combed.

300231169.label: diaper (textile material)
300231169.scope: Self-patterned textile with a small rectilinear pattern formed by contrasting the weave's warp and weft faces.

300231565.label: textile materials
300231565.scope: Materials produced by weaving, felting, knotting, twining, or otherwise processing natural or synthetic fibers so that they cohere into a form or unit; traditionally excludes fiberboard, paper, papier-mâché, and papyrus, which, though also fiber products, are considered as separate types of material. For generic reference to the genre, see "textiles."

300232185.label: tassel
300232185.scope: Pendant trimming, decoration, or garment, comprising loose strands. Before the 20th century, usually a wooden mold covered with strands of silk or worsted; now often merely a bunch of threads, cords, or other strands gathered together at the top.

300232186.label: braid (trimming)
300232186.scope: A narrow trimming made by a variety of techniques such as tablet weaving or braiding. It comes in a variety of fibers and weights, but is heavier than ribbon and flatter than cord.

300234006.label: beads (pierced objects)
300234006.scope: Refers to small objects, of any shape or material, pierced so that they may be strung or hung or attached, as by sewing.

300234144.label: devotional objects
300234144.scope: Use broadly for articles associated with or used in private religious devotions.

300234152.label: silverwork
300234152.scope: Visual works or portions of works fashioned in silver, especially fine, decorative work.

300235443.label: crosses (visual works)
300235443.scope: Visual works in the shape of two intersecting bars, usually an upright one traversed by a horizontal one, especially those used as Christian symbols. For motifs consisting of two intersecting lines, with many variations in the shapes of the arms, use "crosses (motifs)."

300235660.label: bolting cloth
300235660.scope: A firm cloth usually of silk woven in various mesh sizes for various uses such as bolting flour or for use in screen printing or needleworking.

300236072.label: bolsters (soft furnishings)
300236072.scope: Long, often cylindrical, pillows or cushions that are used to support the head of a person lying on a bed, couch, or similar form of furniture.

300236073.label: cushions
300236073.scope: Bags or similar containers made typically of cloth, leather, or rubber stuffed with a resilient material and used to give support or ease to the body while sitting, reclining, or kneeling.

300236074.label: pillows
300236074.scope: Bags or similar containers typically made of cloth that are filled with feathers, down, sponge, or other soft materials and which are used to support the head during sleep or rest.

300236306.label: cosmetics
300236306.scope: Powders, lotion, lipstick, rouge, or other preparations to be applied to the human body for the beautifying, preserving, or altering the appearance of a person.

300236397.label: combs (grooming tools)
300236397.scope: Implements having a row of teeth on one or both edges or sides, used for adjusting, distangling, or cleaning the hair. For such tools that are intended primarily to be decorative and displayed in the hair, use "combs (hair ornaments)."

300236409.label: spectacles (eyeglasses)
300236409.scope: Eyeglasses kept in place by sidepieces passing over the ears.

300236438.label: razors
300236438.scope: Sharp-edged instruments, manually or electrically powered, used especially for shaving the face and legs or trimming hair.

300236484.label: paxes
300236484.scope: Tablets, sometimes of silver, or boards, usually decorated with a Christian religious representation, that is kissed first by the priest and then by members of the congregation.

300236713.label: hairbrushes (grooming tools)
300236713.scope: Brushes for smoothing and styling the hair.

300237754.label: taps (container components)
300237754.scope: Tubular devices inserted into a vessel that permit the outflow of the liquid contents, usually with a spigot to control the rate of the flow.

300239147.label: animal equipment
300239147.scope: Articles, furnishings, or other physical resources utilized for or with animals.

300239260.label: buckles (strap accessories)
300239260.scope: Devices used for fastening consisting of a usually open rectangular or rounded frame and a tongue or catch attached to one side or a vertical bar attached across the center. Sometimes used alone as an ornament.

300239261.label: buttons (fasteners)
300239261.scope: Disks, balls, or devices of other shape having holes or a shank by which they are sewn or secured to an article and that are used as fasteners by passing through a buttonhole or loop or a trimming.

300239307.label: ties (fasteners)
300239307.scope: Cords, bands, or similar flexible devices used for fastening, especially by interlacing, such as in a knot or bow.

300239507.label: clasps (fasteners)
300239507.scope: Fasteners made of two or more parts, often of metal, and consisting of separate interlocking hooking and catching elements that hold together two or more objects or complimentary parts of the same object.

300239965.label: combs (textile working equipment)
300239965.scope: Any of various toothed devices used in handling or ordering textile fibers.

300241583.label: components (objects parts)
300241583.scope: Constituent parts of a larger object. A component differs from an item in that the item can stand alone as an independent work but the component typically cannot or does not stand alone. Examples are a panel of a polyptych or a discrete architectural component such as a dome.

300243428.label: silk (textile)
300243428.scope: Textile made from silk fiber, which is a fiber derived from the cocoon of the silkworm moth.

300243430.label: wool (textile)
300243430.scope: Textile made from the animal hair wool.

300244358.label: counterpanes
300244358.scope: Term formerly used for a variety of bedcovers, especially those woven of cotton or wool; from the mid-19th century onwards generally replaced by the term "bedspreads."

300244387.label: ticks (coverings)
300244387.scope: Cloth cases, usually of ticking, for a bolster, mattress, or pillow, containing feathers, hair, straw, or other materials used for stuffing.

300244578.label: ware
300244578.scope: Refers to a class of manufactured articles, generally of utilitarian type, usually specified by its material, use, style name, or other characteristic, such as ceramic ware or kitchenware. In archaeology, refers to distinct groups of pottery types classified according to characteristics of temper, hardness, type of paste, and surface treatment, rather than by shape or decoration, such as Kamares ware.

300247410.label: cockades
300247410.scope: Rosettes, knots of ribbons, or similar ornaments worn usually on a hat as a badge of office or party, as part of livery dress, or as decoration.

300247420.label: traps (trapping equipment)
300247420.scope: Contrivances used for restraining, isolating, and catching animals; examples include traps having a mechanical device that springs shut suddenly.

300247430.label: rakes (agricultural equipment)
300247430.scope: Implements with teeth or tines for gathering loose plant material, such as cut grass or hay, or for smoothing the surface of the ground. Used in agricultural environments, gardens, landscaping, and other situations.

300247448.label: shipbuilding
300247448.scope: The craft or business of building ships.

300247516.label: handcuffs
300247516.scope: Shackles for the hand, generally consisting of a divided metal ring which is locked around the wrist; usually made in pairs of rings connected by a short chain or bar.

300247544.label: <textile fabricating tools and equipment>
300247544.scope: General term for the class of tools, equipment, and supplies used to facilitate either the processing of natural fibers into thread and yarn or the processing of thread and yarn into finished textile products. Processes encapsulating this class of tools include spinning, weaving, knitting, knotting, twining, and finishing.

300247545.label: sewing tools
300247545.scope: Tools and equipment used for sewing, which uses the process of joining, attaching, or decorating flexible materials with needle and thread.

300247548.label: shuttles (textile fabricating tools)
300247548.scope: Devices of various designs, often a slender bar-like object, used in weaving or netting. In weaving, it passes the thread or yarn of the weft to and from one edge of the cloth to the other between the threads or yarns of the warp.

300247551.label: thimbles
300247551.scope: Small bell-shaped covers worn over the fingertip to protect it when pushing a needle through material in sewing.

300248023.label: remnants
300248023.scope: Use with reference to the unsold or unused end of piece goods.

300248064.label: gold braid
300248064.scope: Any of various gold-colored braids used especially on uniforms.

300248082.label: safes (storage containers)
300248082.scope: Containers for the safe storage of articles; use especially for boxlike receptacles, generally of steel or iron construction and having one or more securing devices, that can be freestanding or built into a wall or vault and which are used to protect money and other valuables against fire or theft. Prefer "kitchen safes" for ventilated cabinets in which food is stored. Prefer "strongboxes" for lockable boxes which tend to be smaller and more portable.

300248085.label: bits (animal work equipment)
300248085.scope: Mouthpieces of bridles, having fittings at each end to which the reins are fastened.

300248092.label: bridles (animal work equiment)
300248092.scope: Headgear with which a horse is governed and restrained, usually consisting of a headstall, bit, and reins.

300248102.label: winnowing baskets
300248102.scope: Baskets used to winnow or separate threshed grain.

300248655.label: tinder
300248655.scope: Any highly flammable dry substance that readily takes spark or fire, typically used to initiate or transfer fire to something else.

300248835.label: crucifixes
300248835.scope: Visual works in the shape of a cross having the figure of Christ crucified.

300249434.label: taffeta
300249434.scope: Crisp textile, typically in plain weave, sometimes with a fine crosswise rib and a smooth lustrous surface on both sides, originally of silk, now of various fibers.

300249437.label: serge
300249437.scope: Durable twill, of worsted or with the warp of worsted and the weft of another wool yarn, with a clear finish and a flat diagonal rib; often used for tailored garments such as suits, coats, and dresses.

300249444.label: lawn (textile)
300249444.scope: Sheer, lightweight plain-woven textile, originally of linen now also of fine combed cotton yarn, filled with starch or sizing. often used for handkerchiefs, aprons, and curtains.

300249660.label: skates (fish)
300249660.scope: General name for various members of nine genera in three families: Rajidae, Arynchobatidae, and Anacanthobatidae, having in common that they are very large, flat, cartilaginous fish often used for food.

300250026.label: apes
300250026.scope: General term denoting any non-human member of the Hominoidea.

300250028.label: monkeys (animals)
300250028.scope: Common term referring to the New World monkeys and the Old World monkeys, two of the three groupings of simian primates, the third of which is the apes. There are over 250 known living species of monkey. Because of their similarity to monkeys, apes are often called "monkeys" in informal usage. Furthermore, some monkey species have the word "ape" in their common name, causing further confusion. Because monkeys are not a single coherent group, they do not all share any particular traits that are not also shared with the apes.

300250047.label: ducks (birds)
300250047.scope: General term for members of various species of relatively small, short-necked, large-billed waterfowl. They differ from geese in being smaller in size and having legs that are placed rearward, and the result is a distinctive waddling gait. Males, known as drakes, and females, known as hens, exhibit some degree of differentiation in plumage and in call.

300250051.label: Falco (genus)
300250051.scope: Members of a genus containing birds of prey characterized by thin, tapered wings that enable them to fly at high speed and to change direction rapidly, plumes called "flags" on their legs, and a notch in their hooked beak called a "tooth."

300250063.label: geese
300250063.scope: General term referring to members of several species of large web-footed birds in different genera, especially the genera Anser and Branta, but also including a number of waterfowl of gooselike build that live in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres and belong to other groups. Geese have in common that they are larger than ducks and smaller than swans; they differ from ducks in having longer necks and legs that are set more forward.

300250116.label: cattle
300250116.scope: A collective term referring to live animals, particularly bovine animals, held as property or reared to serve as meat, or sources of milk, skin, wool, etc.

300250157.label: whales
300250157.scope: General term referring to any of the larger species of marine mammals of the order Cetacea that have fore-limbs like fins and a tail with horizontal flukes, and are hunted for their oil and whalebone.

300250167.label: Mustela erminea (species)
300250167.scope: Members of a species of the weasel family with reddish brown that in winter in northern regions turns wholly white, except the tip of the tail, which is always black. The whiteness of ermine is often a symbol of purity in art and poetry.

300250282.label: oxen
300250282.scope: Castrated adult male cattle, typically used as draft animals.

300250308.label: Cervidae (family)
300250308.scope: Members of a family of ruminants typically having solid antlers that are shed yearly.

300250601.label: squirrels
300250601.scope: General term referring to 122 species in 22 genera of tree squirrels.

300250633.label: porcupines
300250633.scope: General term referring to members of  27 living species in two families of large herbivorous rodents having body and tail covered with sharp defensive spines composed of modified hair.

300250865.label: halibut
300250865.scope: General term referring to several species in different genera of righteyed flounders.

300250867.label: seals (animals)
300250867.scope: General term for any of 32 species of web-footed aquatic mammals that live chiefly in cold seas and whose body shape, round at the middle and tapered at the ends, is adapted to swift and graceful swimming. There are two types of animals often called by this term: the earless, or true, seals (family Phocidae); and the eared seals (family Otariidae), which comprise the sea lions and fur seals.

300250930.label: Pectinidae (family)
300250930.scope: Family of marine bivalves having a radially ribbed shell with undulating edges, and many tiny eyes and feelers on the edge of the mouth; they inhabit sandy sea beds, and can swim by rapidly clapping the shell halve together by means of a single large adductor muscle.

300250954.label: candy
300250954.scope: Foodstuff made from sugar or other sweet, edible substance. Includes a wide variety of forms, from hard lozenges of crystallized sugar made by repeated boiling and slow evaporation, to soft filled sweets, such as chocolate-covered bonbons.

300251631.label: key rings
300251631.scope: Bands in circular or other forms, often in metal, designed to hold keys.

300251746.label: bales (object genre)
300251746.scope: Closely pressed or tightly wrapped, large bundles of materials or goods prepared for storage or transport, as cotton or hay.

300251799.label: paws (animal components)
300251799.scope: The feet of a quadrupedal animal, characterized by being relatively compact feet with pads and claws, often configured so the weight of the animal is placed on the pad and toes rather than on a heel; examples are the feet of a bear, dog, or cat.

300251800.label: tails (animal components)
300251800.scope: The posterior extremities of animals, in position opposite to the head and forming either a distinct flexible appendage to the trunk (e.g., in a dog or cat) or a continuation of the trunk behind the anus (as in a dolphin). In vertebrates, the tail contains an extension of the vertebrae beyond the backbone.

300251844.label: acorns
300251844.scope: Nuts of oak trees and shrubs, growing in a shallow woody cup or cupule.

300253047.label: bands (binding components)
300253047.scope: Raised ridges across the bound spine of a book indicating the location of the cords beneath the covering material. Distinguished from "cords (binding components)," the twisted strands of fibrous material to which the sections of a book are sewn.

300253072.label: bracers
300253072.scope: Protective coverings for the wrist used in archery, fencing, and various ball games, especially those worn by archers on the bow arm as protection from the recoil of the bowstring, generally taking the form of a band, bracelet, or plate.

300253474.label: buckram
300253474.scope: Heavy weave cotton, jute, or linen textile stiffened with glue, size, or starch and used for interlinings in garments, box making,  bookbinding, etc.

300253844.label: Capreolus capreolus (species)
300253844.scope: Members of a species of relatively small Eurasian deer found in small family groups in lightly forested regions.

300253876.label: waste
300253876.scope: Left-over or superfluous material or by-product not useful to the work or process at hand, as from construction, printing, manufacturing, or industry.

300254496.label: food
300254496.scope: Any material that can be digested or absorbed by the body of a human or other animal and used as a source of energy or some essential nutrient, to build and replace tissue, or to relieve hunger.

300254615.label: cauls (headgear)
300254615.scope: Close-fitting caps or hairnets usually of gold, silver, silk, or wool thread, often decorated with pearls or beads and made to confine hair; worn by women and sometimes by men especially during the 13th through the 16th century. For hairnets used to confine hair at the back of the neck or attached to the back edge of a hat, use "snoods."

300254740.label: packing material
300254740.scope: Any material used to protect, cushion, or brace objects for safe shipment or storage. For packing material that carries information or otherwise conveys a message about the product, use "packaging."

300254861.label: lampas (textile material)
300254861.scope: Woven textile material characterized by a weave structure that uses a secondary or binding warp to bind the wefts that form the design, producing a double weave effect.

300255019.label: cake (food)
300255019.scope: Any of a variety of sweet, relatively rich quick breads, shortened or unshortened, typically made with flour, sugar, leavening, liquid, and flavoring, and usually shaped by the tin in which it is baked.

300255555.label: whips (striking tools)
300255555.scope: Instruments consisting of an often rigid handle and a flexible lash or lashes made of cord or leather, used for disciplinary action, torture, or weapons against animals or humans.

300255573.label: stirrups
300255573.scope: Metal, wooden, or leather devices with a flat foot rest and bow-shaped section attached to the saddle by a stirrup strap, used to support the rider's feet.

300255580.label: collars (horse collars)
300255580.scope: The curved parts of harnesses, shaped to fit around a draft animal's neck, against which it exerts its weight to move a load.

300256164.label: sumac (wood)
300256164.scope: Wood of trees belonging to the genus Rhus. Since they are usually shrubs or very small trees, it is more common for the trees to be used for tannin and other products than for wood.

300256296.label: saddle blankets
300256296.scope: Blankets, often woolen, placed between a saddle and a horse's back when riding.

300256941.label: fishing floats
300256941.scope: Devices made of buoyant materials, tied onto a line or net when fishing to gauge the depth of the fishhook or net.

300257145.label: mudfishes
300257145.scope: General term for fish of various species in various orders that live in mud, whether marine, estuarine, or freshwater.

300257158.label: fishing lines
300257158.scope: Lines for catching fish, varying in diameter and weight depending on the fish sought and the method of angling.

300257285.label: state (creative stage)
300257285.scope: Refers to the variant stages of development of graphic and textual works.

300257363.label: horse blankets
300257363.scope: Cloth coverings of various materials cut to cover a horse's body from around the withers to the rump and, in front, around the chest; used to protect a horse or discourage growth of a heavy coat.

300257519.label: linens (textile works)
300257519.scope: Collectively, the items for the bed and table made of linen or other similar fabrics; may also be used for clothing made of linen from the Medieval period through the 19th century.

300258665.label: tabards
300258665.scope: Short sleeveless or short-sleeved garments consisting of front and back panels and open at the sides, worn over other garments, sometimes to display heraldic devices, by knights, heralds, or civilians, especially during the 12th to the 14th centuries. For padded or quilted protective garments worn over metal armor embellished with heraldic devices, use "coat armors."

300258857.label: fans (costume accessories)
300258857.scope: Implements used to produce a current of air for individual use; also objects in the form of such implements, but intended to serve as ceremonial or decorative accessories; may be rigid or collapsible. The operation of the fan may be done by oneself or the fan may be held by another to benefit the recipient.

300258901.label: baldrics
300258901.scope: Bands, sashes, or belts, usually richly ornamented, worn diagonally from shoulder to hip to support a dagger, bugle, sword, or drum.

300261225.label: Anguilliformes (order)
300261225.scope: Members of an order containing 19 families, 110 genera, and almost 600 species of fresh water and marine soft-finned bony fishes with elongated snake-like or worm-like bodies.

300261263.label: salmon (fish)
300261263.scope: General term for several species in different genera in the family Salmonidae, found in both the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, as well as in the Great Lakes and other land locked lakes. Most species are salt water fish that spawn in fresh water.

300261825.label: cordovan (leather)
300261825.scope: Soft, durable, fine-grained, nonporous colored leather, vegetable-tanned and curried, made originally solely from the outer layer of horsehide rumps, later also from goatskin and pigskin.

300262203.label: fire screens (equipment)
300262203.scope: Protective screens made of woven or linked metal or other nonflammable material, placed in front of fireplace openings to prevent logs, sparks, or embers from escaping. For furniture used to protect occupants of the room from the full heat of the fire, use "fire screens (furniture)."

300262572.label: writing tablets (information artifacts)
300262572.scope: Hand-held, flat objects used for writing or drawing, either directly, or as a flat, rigid support for another surface such as paper. If written upon directly, the tablets are typically coated with a substance such as clay, plaster, or wax upon which the characters or depictions are incised with a stylus.

300262797.label: buoys
300262797.scope: Moored, floating devices, employed as aids to mariners, marking navigable limits of channels and their fairways, or hazards such as sunken dangers, rocks, mines, torpedoe grounds or telegraph cables.

300262820.label: bread
300262820.scope: Use generally for cooked food made of dough composed of flour or meal of various plants, water, and other ingredients, with or without the addition of a leavening agent. Use specifically for loaves or cakes of dough made with flour and cooked by baking.

300262831.label: rosaries
300262831.scope: Refers to strings of beads or knotted cord used for a religious exercise in which prayers are recited and counted on the beads or knots. The term is most often used to refer to strings of beads used in Roman Catholicism and Eastern Orthodoxy, although it may also be used to refer to prayer beads employed in Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, and other religions. In Christianity, the practice was adopted in the 3rd century by Eastern Christian monks, and various forms of the rosary were developed. In Roman Catholicism, the rosary became a popular method of public and private prayer. The most common rosary is the rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary, comprising beads arranged in five decades (sets of 10), each decade separated from the next by a larger bead. The two ends of the string are joined by a smaller string holding a crucifix, two large beads, and three small beads. The devotions consist of the recitation or chanting of fifteen decades of Aves, each decade being preceded by a Paternoster and followed by a Gloria.

300262951.label: mummies (bodies)
300262951.scope: Refers the bodies of human beings, or sometimes of animals, that have been embalmed, naturally preserved, or treated for burial with preservatives. Among the many peoples who practiced mummification were the people living along the Torres Strait between Papua New Guinea and Australia, the Incas of South America, and the Chinese. Prominent examples were created by the ancient Egyptians. The process varied from age to age in Egypt, but it always involved removing the internal organs (though in a late period they were replaced after treatment), treating the body with resin, and wrapping it in linen bandages.

300263094.label: split (animal material)
300263094.scope: Any one of two or more layers of a skin or hide separated from each other by a mechanical splitting process.

300263278.label: spinning wheels
300263278.scope: Machines for turning fiber into thread or yarn, in which the formation of the thread is performed by the help of a wheel worked either by a hand or foot pedal that spins the thread onto a single spindle. Said to have been invented in India, they were introduced into Europe via the Middle East in the Medieval period, and were in common use there and in North America after colonization into the 18th century. For spinning machines developed in the 18th century having more than one spindle, use "spinning jennies."

300263565.label: deerskin
300263565.scope: Skin of a deer or other member of the cervid family, used especially for clothing, moccasins, and bookbinding leather. In early bookbinding, before the 16th century, the skin was either processed with lime or alum-tawed to make it white in appearance. For processed deerskin, use "buckskin" or "doeskin (skin)."

300263571.label: law sheep
300263571.scope: Smooth-grained natural- or cream-colored sheepskin leather, vegetable-tanned, usually with bark, commonly used in the 19th and early 20th centuries in binding law books, especially in England, as a less expensive alternative to "law calf." It has been superceded in that use by "law buckram."

300263573.label: forel
300263573.scope: Parchment made from sheepskin, dressed in imitation of vellum. It is not strong and tends to be greasy.

300263678.label: rings (object genres)
300263678.scope: Circular objects made of various materials and in various sizes, used in many different contexts and applications.

300263795.label: distaffs
300263795.scope: Tools used for holding prepared fibers in a carefully arranged manner so that they require the minimum of manual regulation during spinning.

300264024.label: embroidery (visual works)
300264024.scope: Refers to works characterized by a pattern or design executed in stitches using thread or fine wire. The designs are typically executed on textiles, but leather, paper, or another media may also be used; the designs may be intended to be framed, or to decorate apparel, bed linens, furniture coverings, pillows, altar cloths, ceremonial hangings, or other items.

300264248.label: clove (flower bud)
300264248.scope: Small, reddish-brown flower bud of the tropical evergreen tree Syzygium aromaticum. It yields oil which is used as an antiseptic and a flavoring, and is dried and ground into an aromatic spice. The ground flower is also used as a means of organic pest control.

300264317.label: blotters (writing equipment)
300264317.scope: Pieces of blotting paper in various sizes and formats, including individual sheets, gatherings of sheets, and large sheets inserted or built into desk pads to protect desk tops from ink stains.

300264331.label: haberdasheries
300264331.scope: The goods for men sold at a haberdasher's shop or store department, such as shirts, ties, socks, belts, hats, gloves. and other accessories.

300264388.label: pictures (object genre)
300264388.scope: Object genre that includes two-dimensional works. Examples would be in the media of painting, drawing, photography, film, digital formats, bas-relief, or other media. In usage, the term does not necessarily imply that the work is representational, but instead refers to the two dimensionality of the work, including abstract works. However, it excludes purely decorative details; for example, a faux-marble painted, decorative wall panel is not considered a picture. To particularly designate works that represent the visible world, use "depictions(visual works)" or "representation (form of expression)." In historical usage, "pictures" was typically reserved for paintings; in modern usage, use "paintings (visual works)" to designate paintings in particular.

300264606.label: timber (wood by form)
300264606.scope: Wood in the form of large, squared or dressed pieces used for forming part of a built work or used to create a curving frame branching outward from the keel of a ship and bending upward in a vertical direction. Timber that is curved or bent may be a composite formed of several pieces rather than being a single piece of wood.

300264628.label: mills (equipment)
300264628.scope: Refers to machines or mechanical apparatus, either simple or complex, for grinding or reducing a solid substance to a powder or pulp, such as corn or spice. To refer to the combined building and the milling machinery housed within it, use "mills (buildings)."

300264821.label: printed ephemera
300264821.scope: Printed works that are created to meet an array of immediate needs, usually transitory in nature not intended to be saved. Examples cold be broadsides, posters, leaflets, pamphlets, programs, postcards, tradecards, labels, tickets, handbills, sale notices, and valentines.

300264831.label: gold leaf
300264831.scope: Refers to sheets of gold that have been hammered or rolled very thin (typically around 0.1 micrometer, or 4 millionths of an inch, thick). In art, gold leaf has been applied to paintings, sculptures, manuscripts, and decorative arts since around 1500 BCE. In the 1920s, the process of creating gold leaf was successfully automated.

300264860.label: sickles
300264860.scope: Agricultural implements consisting of a hook-shaped metal blade with a short handle fitted on a tang. Similar in form and use to  'reaping hooks,' but distinguished from these by having serrated cutting edges, and the method in which they are employed.

300264929.label: sprinkler flasks
300264929.scope: Bottles made to allow the sprinkling of perfume, water, or another liquid that must be dispensed parsimoniously. One construction utilizes a neck resembling a washer: the constriction regulates the flow of contents to a trickle. Among other forms are nipple-like or tapering or branched tops perforated with holes. Contents were luxury items such as expensive perfumes, rose water, or in the church, holy water. Sprinkler flasks are found in ancient Egypt, China, the Middle East, the ancient Roman world, Europe, and North America.

300265121.label: metalware
300265121.scope: Articles made of metal, especially utensils and tableware.

300265199.label: silver leaf
300265199.scope: Silver beaten out into thin leaf for use in gilding. Silver leaf is about three times as thick as gold leaf because silver is less malleable but the resulting leaf is easier to handle. It requires lacquering or varnishing to prevent tarnishing; for this reason it is often replaced by palladium leaf. In the commerical arts inexpensive aluminum leaf is used to achieve the effect of silver leaf. Silver leaf can also be covered with a golden yellow transparent coating as a substitute for gold.

300265255.label: antependia
300265255.scope: Panels or hangings for the front of a Christian altar, pulpit, or lectern; may be carved, painted, embroidered, or otherwise decorated. Antependia are of various materials including wood, ivory, precious metals, and embroidered textiles. The exposed position of precious antependia meant that they were sometimes moved on top of the altar for safety, thus becoming retables. If the coverings are continued around the sides and back they are called "paraments" or paliotti.

300265413.label: pasta (food)
300265413.scope: Paste or dough made of water and flour into various forms such as macaroni, spaghetti, and vermicelli; it can be dried for use later or made fresh.

300265591.label: incense (material by function)
300265591.scope: Grains or pieces of gum and sometimes spices that are burned to produce a fragrant odor. Incense is frequently used as an oblation, or in religious ritual. The term can also refer to the smoke produced by the burning of incense.

300265716.label: Felidae (family)
300265716.scope: Family of mammals containing 37 species in 18 genera representing the cheetah, puma, jaguar, leopard, lion, lynx, tiger, domestic cat, and others, descended from a common ancestor about 10.8 million years ago. According to a 2006 genomic study the ancestor of extant Leopardus, Lynx, Puma, Prionailurus, and Felis lineages migrated across the Bering land bridge into the Americas approximately 8 to 8.5 million years ago. Members of Felidae are typically characterized by having a long tail, a head with a short nose and round face, large eyes positioned for good binocular vision, usually with short ears, sharp claws that are retractile except in the cheetah, a tongue covered with horny papillae, five toes on their forefeet and four on their hindfeet, with the male larger than the female, possessing a genetic anomaly that prevents them from tasting sweetness, and being the most strictly carnivorous of the mammal families in the order Carnivora. Their closest relatives are thought to be the civets, hyenas, and mongooses.

300265717.label: Felis (genus)
300265717.scope: Genus of six Old World species, including the wildcat and domestic cat.

300265738.label: spindles (textile working equipment)
300265738.scope: Rods, usually tapered at both ends, used as axes in hand spinning. Fibers are drawn and twisted onto the spindle from a mass of wool or other material that is gathered on the distaff. The image of the spindle and distaff has been associated historically with feminine power or virtue. For the similar cylindrical objects used to gather or accumulate thread after it has been spun, and for use in weaving, use "spools."

300265977.label: Equus (genus)
300265977.scope: Genus including horses and similar animals. It evolved from small animals with multi-toed padded hooves. Equus is the only surviving genus in the once diverse family of horses. It was domesticated about 3,000 years ago.

300266085.label: fish (animals)
300266085.scope: General term referring to animals from several evolutionary lines and thus not properly a taxonomic group. The term refers to aquatic animals found in the fresh and salt waters all over the world, characterized by being cold-blooded, living and breathing primarily in the water throughout their lives, possessing gill slits, a notochord or skeletal supporting rod, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, a tail, scales covering the body, and two sets of paired fins and several unpaired fins. Living species range from the primitive jawless lampreys and hagfishes through the jawed fishes with cartilaginous skeletons such as sharks, skates, and rays to the abundant and diverse bony fishes.

300266122.label: trinkets
300266122.scope: Refers to small ornaments, typically showy inexpensive jewelry or other articles for personal adornment or attached to clothing.

300266222.label: ambergris
300266222.scope: A waxy, odorous substance of marbled ashy color produced in the intestines of the sperm whale, and often found floating in tropical seas, or on the seashore. Formerly used as an ingredient in perfumery to prevent evaporation, more recently it has been replaced in this function by synthetic substances.

300266236.label: massicot
300266236.scope: Heavy yellow powder composed of lead monoxide, both the native mineral as well as lead monoxide produced by heating lead carbonate to 300 C. It is used as a drier in oil, as a low-fire flux in making ceramics and glass, as a yellow pigment in paints and glazes, in thin layers to produce iridescent colors on brass and bronze, as a filler for rubber, and to produce artificial tortoiseshell and horn.

300266272.label: peaches (fruits)
300266272.scope: Refers to the large round, juicy, single-seeded fruits of a smallish tree belonging to the genus Prunus persica, believed to have originated in China, and cultivated in warmer climates throughout the world. The fruit has yellow or whitish flesh, a delicate aroma, and a skin that is either velvety (peaches) or smooth (nectarines) in different cultivars. Peaches are known in for the many associated folk tales and traditions, including that it was said to be consumed by the immortals, conferring longevity on all who ate them.

300266417.label: apples (fruits)
300266417.scope: The fruit of trees in the Malus genus. Domestic apples are usually green, red, or yellow, cultivated in temperate zones worldwide in a multitude of varieties.

300266423.label: lemons (fruits)
300266423.scope: Citrus fruits with an oval shape, yellow skin, with acidic, juicy pulp.

300266426.label: walnuts (nuts)
300266426.scope: Fruits (drupaceous nuts) from any of several species of walnut tree, having a two-lobed seed covered with a fleshy husk.

300266428.label: chestnuts (nuts)
300266428.scope: Nuts of the chestnut tree, two or more of which are inclosed in a prickly 'burr.'

300266440.label: olives (fruits)
300266440.scope: Oval drupe, or stone-fruit, of the olive tree. The edible olive has been cultivated since approximately 3500 BCE, generally in warm climates. There are hundreds of named varieties.

300266452.label: molasses (syrup)
300266452.scope: The thick, brown, uncrystallized syrup drained from raw sugar, particularly the concentrated syrup obtained from sugar during the process of refining from cane or beet juice.

300266506.label: Aves (class)
300266506.scope: The class of vertebrate animals that are typically bipedal and warm-blooded, lay large-yolked hardshelled eggs, often arboreal, and possessing feathers, hollow bones, forelimbs adapted for flight (although some have lost the ability to fly) and hindlimbs for perching and locomotion, a four-chambered heart, keen vision, a horny beak without teeth, and a large muscular stomach. Birds arose from theropod dinosaurs, which were an order of carnivorous dinosaurs.

300266516.label: Ursidae (family)
300266516.scope: Family containing nine species in six genera, characterized as being large, short-tailed, having stocky legs, a long snout, shaggy hair, and plantigrade paws with five non-retractile claws. Bears are generally omnivorous, but some bears are entirely carnivorous (like the polar bear ) or vegetarian (like the panda).

300266520.label: foxes (animals)
300266520.scope: General term referring to various members of the family Canidae, especially those of the genus Vulpes, such as the red or common, fox (V. vulpes), which lives in both the Old World and the New World. Several other foxes belong to genera other than Vulpes, including the North American gray fox, the Arctic fox, and the the bat-eared fox, and the crab-eating fox. Foxes resemble small dogs, with pointed snouts, large ears, and bushy tails.

300266639.label: clothing
300266639.scope: Coverings for the torso, limbs, hands, feet, and head for warmth, fashion, or to cover nudity. It generally excludes other items of costume such as jewelry, crowns, and other accessories that are purely decorative or symbolic and have no practical function.

300266770.label: footstones (tombstones)
300266770.scope: Refers to the upright stones placed at the foot of graves, that is, over the feet of the interred body, generally shorter in height than the headstone.

300266794.label: ornaments (object genre)
300266794.scope: Decorative forms or embellishments that are an integral part of a building or object but are not essential to its structure. Refers also to decorative objects attached to or worn by humans and animals. For objects signifying an honor bestowed upon an individual, usually worn on the person, see "decorations." Regarding techniques of embellishment in general, see "decoration (process)."

300298735.label: Agnus Deis (medallions)
300298735.scope: Refers to disks of wax bearing the sign of the Agnus Dei, which is a symbol of Christ in the form of a lamb bearing a cross with a halo round its head. The small cake of wax was stamped with such a figure and blessed by the Pope. The wax may be the remains of the Pascal candle, solemnly blessed by the Pope on the Thursday after Easter. Disks may be round or oval. Figures of saints or the name and arms of the Pope are commonly impressed on the reverse. Agnus Deis may be worn suspended round the neck, or they may be preserved as objects of devotion. In virtue of the consecration they receive, they are regarded as "sacramentals," like holy water or blessed palms.

300298764.label: portable altars
300298764.scope: Altars that are of relatively small size and transportable, often fitting into a container along with other items for worship or services. In Christian contexts, examples include consecrated altar stones set in a case or otherwise mounted, used by priests who travel from location to location saying Mass where a permanent consecrated altar may not be available. Specifications included that it should be a solid piece of natural stone of a type and size resistant to fracture, consecrated by a bishop, large enough to hold the host and chalice, and designed so that it may be inserted in or placed on a table convenient for the service. For transportable versions of Christian painted or carved image-bearing objects of the type displayed on or above an altar, use "portable altarpieces."

300298908.label: aspergilla
300298908.scope: Instruments, usually of metal attached to an absorbent material, for the sprinkling of holy water. In the Western church, the aspergillum is composed of a handle surmounted by a perforated ball, sponge, or brush-like end to hold water. Some have sponges or internal reservoirs that dispense holy water when shaken, while others must periodically be dipped in "aspersoriums (vessels)." The tool was originally made of branches of hyssop, palm, or boxwood, wisps of straw, or the tail of a fox (in Old French the fox was called "goupil"). By the 13th century the aspergillum assumed the modern Western form of a handle surmounted by a rose-shape covered with bristles; the handles of the sprinklers came to be very richly ornamented. In the Greek Orthodox Church the aspergillum is a standing vessel with a tapering lid perforated with holes for sprinkling; in the Russian Orthodox Church, it is a whisk made of cloth, hair, or sprigs of basil. The tool was derived from ancient sources, where branches were used to sprinkle water, blood, or another liquid in rituals. Such tools were used in ancient Rome, the Middle East, ancient Norse rituals, and elsewhere.

300298934.label: aurifrisia
300298934.scope: Borders of particularly rich embroidery or woven designs in gold thread and colored silk, often embellished with jewels or beads, used as ornamental bands on clothing, such as on royal or ecclesiastical vestments. Term refers to the Phrygians, who were noted for their skill in embroidering with gold.

300299039.label: ceremonial maces
300299039.scope: Maces intended primarily for ceremonial display rather than as weapons. A ceremonial mace is a staff or club-shaped device, often richly ornamented and typically topped with a knob or other head-piece, carried by priestly officials, ecclesiastical persons, magistrates, and academic persons as a symbol of jurisdiction or office during a solemn ceremony. Examples are found in ancient Egypt, pre-Columbian America, Asia, and Europe and North America. For similar objects carried by rulers, use "scepters."

300299206.label: shirts of mail
300299206.scope: Protective garments often used as armor, in the form of a shirt, covering the torso and made of mail, which is metal fabric consisting of iron or steel rings riveted or pressed together.

300299255.label: candle sconces
