300299255.scope: Wall-mounted candelabra or other supports specifically for candles and intended to be mounted on a wall.

300302722.label: beer (beverage)
300302722.scope: An alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of malt from cereal grain (or another saccharine substance), flavored with hops or other aromatic bitters. Formerly the term was used as distinct from "ale," with beer being hopped; now "ale" is used to describe a type of beer. May also be applied as a generic reference to other fermented liquors of various kinds, flavored by various ingredients such as ginger.

300310341.label: Viverridae (family)
300310341.scope: Family containing 35 species in 20 genera of civets and related species resembling long-nosed cats, having retractile or partially-retractile claws, a baculum (penile bone), and an anal scent gland. They are among the most primitive families Carnivora, with skeletons very similar to those of fossils dating back to the Eocene 50 million years ago.

300310364.label: Leopardus (genus)
300310364.scope: Genus of three primarily Central and South American species, including the little spotted cat, margay, and ocelot.

300310470.label: Insecta (class)
300310470.scope: Members of a class containing over 1,000,000 species characerized by a body divided into head, thorax, and abdomen; head with one pair of antennae, mouthparts consisting of a pair of mandibles and two pairs of maxillae, several pairs of legs, and often wings.

300310568.label: badgers (animals)
300310568.scope: General term referring to members of ten or more species of stout carnivores of the weasel family, found in various parts of the world, known for their burrowing ability, and some having one or more white stripes on their heads. The species differ in size, habitat, and coloration, but all are nocturnal and possess anal scent glands, powerful jaws, and large, heavy claws on their forefeet, which are used to dig for food and construct underground dens.

300311202.label: sealing wax
300311202.scope: Resinous preparation of shellac and turpentine, or of beeswax and Venice turpentine with coloring matter, that is plastic when warm and used for sealing letters, attaching impressions of seals to documents, and sealing batteries and jars.

300311362.label: earth color (pigment)
300311362.scope: Paint pigments prepared by grinding minerals containing iron oxides and other materials such as clay, chalk, and silica. Each deposit has a unique composition, working characteristics, and color, in varying ranges of yellow, orange, red, brown, and black. Earth colors have been used since prehistoric times and are permanent in all techniques. Synthetic iron oxides, called Mars colors, have been produced since the late 18th century.

300311365.label: mustard (material)
300311365.scope: Pungent yellow powder of the seeds of any of several common mustard plants, used as a condiment, dye, or in medicine as a stimulant and diuretic, an emetic, or a counterirritant.

300311394.label: green bice (pigment)
300311394.scope: Unstandardized term referring to several green pigments, including pigment created by adding yellow orpiment to smalt, pigment comprising synthetic copper carbonate, pigment comprising natural copper carbonate created by grinding the mineral malachite, green earth pigment, and viridian pigment.

300311550.label: blue bice (pigment)
300311550.scope: Unstandardiized pigment name for several materials, including the synthetic copper carbonate (blue verditer), pigment produced from grinding the copper carbonate mineral azurite, smalt pigment, and others.

300311590.label: Armenian bole
300311590.scope: Soft red ocher that is a natural mixture of hydrated silicate clays colored with red iron oxide. Since at least the 17th century, it has been used as a foundation for gold leaf and as a red earth pigment.

300312262.label: statuettes (free-standing sculpture)
300312262.scope: Three-dimensional, free-standing sculptures that are smaller than life-size and usually but not always figural. They are often reduced versions of larger works. While the term may be used interchangeably with "figurine" in certain situations, it differs in that a statuette is always free-standing while a figurine may be part of a larger work, such as a decorative detail on a candelabra or mirror. Also, a statuette may represent objects other than a figure, while a figurine always represents a human, animal, or mythical figure.

300312277.label: pilches
300312277.scope: Infants' garments worn over a diaper, usually triangular wrappers made of flannel, boiled wool, or tightly knitted wool, used in Western nations until the 1890s when more waterproof materials such as rubberized cloth were available. In modern usage, the term is sometimes used to refer to colorful pants lined with plastic or other waterproof material and used to cover infants' diapers. The term also refers to earlier outer garments for adults, made of animal skin with the fur turned inside and used as a lining.

300312364.label: sacks (generic containers)
300312364.scope: Large, flexible containers made from flax, hemp, another textile, or plastic, oblong in shape, open at one end, and used for storing, transporting, or carrying corn, flour, fruit, potatoes, wood, coal, or other such items. For containers or receptacles of leather, cloth, paper, or other flexible material capable of being closed at the mouth, use "bags (general containers)."

300343602.label: Iris (genus)
300343602.scope: Genus comprising around 300 species of flowering plants; from the Greek word for a rainbow, referring to the wide variety of flower colors found among species. Irises are natives of Europe, northern Africa, and temperate regions of Asia and America; most species have tuberous (less commonly bulbous or fibrous) roots, sword-shaped equitant leaves, and showy flowers.

300343670.label: Santalum album (species)
300343670.scope: Species of long-lived, woody, flowering plant; the most commonly known source of sandalwood. This species has been long valued, harvested, and cultivated for its fragrant wood and medicinal qualities of essential oil. Currently, the wild population is vulnerable to extinction; very few sizable trees exist, thus it is not currently much used for fine woodworking; harvest of new trees is viable only after 40 years.

300343822.label: painted glass (visual works)
300343822.scope: Works done by painting on the front or the reverse of glass, including with vitrified pigments. In the context of stained glass windows and panels, refers to parts of the image that are painted on glass (often stained glass), especially the smaller details. Also includes works on flat surfaces, vessels, and other types of works. Painted glass mirrors and other glass decoration, and painted works in the manner of painting on canvas or wooden panels were known since ancient times.  [painted glass, not same as stained glass]

300343896.label: Cinnamomum (genus)
300343896.scope: Genus containing around 350 species of tree and shrub, including those having bark from which the spice cinnamon is derived.

300374826.label: brazilwood dye
300374826.scope: Red dye produced from the hot water extraction of any of several tropical trees of the Caesalpinia genus. Its principal colorant is brasilin, a hydroxyanthraquinone. Used to dye textiles as early as the 12th century in Europe; the color is not lightfast and fades when heated.

300374995.label: bay laurel (wood)
300374995.scope: Wood the species Laurus nobilis native to the Mediterranean region; used for small novelties, carving, and marquetry.

300375000.label: Citrus (genus)
300375000.scope: Genus of plants that includes the citron, lemon, lime, orange, grapefruit, tangerine, shaddock, and their many varieties, most yielding pulpy fruits covered with fairly thick skins. The genus is believed to have originated in southeast Asia; citrus has been cultivated in an increasingly large area since ancient times. The precise number of natural species is unclear and their taxonomy is complex because many of the named species are clonally propagated hybrids. There is genetic evidence that even some wild breeding species are of hybrid origin: cultivated citrus may be derived from as few as four ancestral species.

300375054.label: heads (animal components)
300375054.scope: The anterior parts of the body of humans and animals containing the mouth, special sense organs such as the eyes, nose, and ears, and the brain; typically separated by a neck or otherwise distinguished from the rest of the body.

300375063.label: gall (plant material)
300375063.scope: Material made of excrescences produced on trees, usually the oak species Quercus infectoria in Europe and the Near East, and on the sumac species Rhus semialata in China and Japan, by the action of insects, chiefly of the genus Cynips. Galls are formed when gall-wasp eggs are deposited on tree branches in nut-like pockets; the gall grows until the larvae are completely enveloped. The mature insect bores a hole through the gall in order to escape. All galls contain 36-60% tannins; the bluish-green galls, gathered before the insect escapes, are richest in gallotannic acid. The tannins have been used for centuries for vegetable tanning of leather. When galls are combined with ferrous sulfate, a black dye is produced; alone, they produce a gray dye. Gall extract was also used as a mordant in the preparation of writing inks.

300375070.label: Reseda luteola (species)
300375070.scope: Species of flowering plant native of Eurasia, and introduced to North America where it has become a weed. Source of natural yellow dye.

300375265.label: kindling
300375265.scope: Combustible material used for starting fires.

300375396.label: Calamus (genus)
300375396.scope: Genus containing around 325 species of palms.

300375399.label: buds (plant components)
300375399.scope: Small projections located at the axil of a leaf, composed of tiny leaves resembling scales, and forming the rudiment of a branch, cluster of leaves, or blossom. Applied to a flower or leaf at any stage of growth until fully opened.

300375400.label: Syzygium (genus)
300375400.scope: Genus comprising around 1100 species of flowering plants, native from Africa and Madagascar through southern Asia east through the Pacific.

300375485.label: Cyperus (genus)
300375485.scope: Genus containing around 650 species of annual or perennial plants distributed throughout all continents, often in wetlands. The stems are circular or triangular in cross-section, usually leafless for most of their length with the slender grass-like leaves at the base of the plant.

300375537.label: Ceratonia siliqua (species)
300375537.scope: Species of tree native to the eastern Mediterranean region and cultivated elsewhere. It is highly drought resistant. The tree reaches about 15 m (50 feet) in height, has glossy evergreen leaves, and produces long leathery pods that contain up to 15 hard brown seeds embedded in a sweet, edible pulp. The ripened pods are food for animals and also ground for a variety of uses by humans. The seeds are ground to produce a gum. The seeds were a standard of weight measurement in the ancient world, from which the concept "carat" is derived. The common names referring to locusts or St. John's bread come from the belief that the so-called "locusts" on which John the Baptist fed in the Biblical story were carob pods, not grasshoppers. There are various other references to the tree in the Bible.

300375600.label: balm of Gilead
300375600.scope: Fragrant myrrhlike oleoresin obtained from the small evergreen tree, Commiphora opobalsamum, native to the Middle East. Used in perfumes and medicines. Referred to in biblical Genesis as a healing balm; valued in medicine and perfume in ancient Greece and the Roman Empire. The term "balm of Gilead" has been incorrectly used to refer to "Canada balsam," which is derived from a North American tree.

300375603.label: turpentine (resin)
300375603.scope: A sticky, viscous yellow sap obtained from conifers. The crude turpentine contains about 65 percent rosin (solid residue) and 18 percent oil of turpentine (volatile portion). It is distilled to create the volatile oil of turpentine, usually shortened to "turpentine (oil)."

300375614.label: Styrax (genus)
300375614.scope: Genus containing around 120 species of shrubs or small trees native to warm temperate and tropical regions of the Northern Hemisphere, in eastern and southeastern Asia and South America.

300375689.label: counter tables
300375689.scope: Tables on which monetary calculations were made using tokens or counters on a checkered background, similar in usage to an abacus. Often having a compartment beneath for money, tokens, and goods.

300375744.label: fur stoles
300375744.scope: Lengths of fur or furs, sewn together in a way to allow them to be wrapped and carried about the shoulders or arms.  A fur stole is often the pelage or skin of a single animal (head included).

300379003.label: decorations (ornamental works)
300379003.scope: Embellishments, adornments, or ornamentation, often specifically those that are temporarily put up on a holiday or another special occasion.

300379004.label: angels (spirits)
300379004.scope: Generic term for ministering spirits or divine messengers known in several theologies, forming an order of spiritual beings superior to man in power and intelligence. In Jewish, Christian, Islamic, and other theologies, the attendants and messengers of the Deity.

300379033.label: antidotes
300379033.scope: Remedies to counteract the effects of a poison, toxin, or an attack of disease. Administered by mouth, intravenously, or sometimes on the skin, antidotes work by causing an opposite effect in the body, whether directly neutralizing the poison, binding to the poison to prevent its absorption, or otherwise inactivating it or blocking its action.

300379102.label: yards (measurements)
300379102.scope: Units of length comprising 3 feet or 36 inches; by international agreement in 1959 standardized as exactly 0.9144 meters.

300379166.label: beaters (striking tools)
300379166.scope: Tools used to pound, hammer, or tap materials to be flattened or mashed. The term is extended in particular to wooden tools used to pound the bark or bast of trees in the manufacture of bark cloth in African and Oceanic cultures.

300379234.label: rods (measurements)
300379234.scope: Measurements of length equal to 5.5 yards, 16.5 feet, or about 5.03 meters. Also used as area measurements where square rods are equal to 30.25 square yards or about 25.3 square meters. Rods are also called poles or perches.

300379351.label: claws (animal components)
300379351.scope: Sharp, horny, narrow, arched structures on the digits of birds, reptiles, many mammals, and some amphibians. Claws are composed of hardened (keratinized) modifications of the epidermis. Claws may be adapted for scratching, clutching, digging, or climbing. The term is also used for similar structures on the feet of insects, crustacea, and other lower animals.

300379442.label: wine
300379442.scope: Alcoholic beverage made from fermented grapes. The term has been used for beverages made from other fermented plants.

300379595.label: unicorns
300379595.scope: Fabulous and legendary animals usually regarded as having the body of a horse with a single horn projecting from the forehead. The unicorn has at various times been identified or confused with the rhinoceros, with various species of antelope, or with other animals having a horns or a horn-like projection from the head. The horn of the narwhal was passed off as unicorn horn; the unicorn horn was valuable, reputed to possess medicinal or magical properties

300379646.label: bismuth
300379646.scope: Pure metallic element having as symbol Bi. Bismuth is brittle with a low melting point; a grayish-white lustrous metal oxidized by air. It is chiefly used in the arts as an alloy, as in bronze, and is used ground as a pigment.

300379741.label: Streptopelia turtur (species)
300379741.scope: Migratory species of slim dove native to Africa, Asia, and Europe.

300379750.label: quails
300379750.scope: General term for several genera of mid-sized birds in the Galliformes order, in the families Phasianidae and Odontophoridae.

300379800.label: hawks (bird)
300379800.scope: General term for various small to medium-sized falconiform birds, most in the families Accipitridae and Falconidae.

300379825.label: concretion
300379825.scope: A mass of aggregated mineral matter found in sedimentary rocks, usually around a nucleus.

300379869.label: drugs
300379869.scope: Substances of animal, vegetable, mineral, or synthetic origin that are used as an ingredient in pharmacy, in the prevention or treatment of disease, as a medicine, or to otherwise obtain a physiological effect on a living organism. Also includes substances having intoxicating, stimulant, or narcotic effects.

300379948.label: tiles (object genre)
300379948.scope: Relatively small, flat objects, often rectangular, used to cover roofs, floors or walls, as game pieces, as lids, or for other purposes. Originally referred to such objects made of baked earth or earthenware, but modern usage includes such items made of other materials, including metal or plastic.

300379961.label: pomegranates (fruits)
300379961.scope: Fruit of Punica granatum, a bush or small tree of Asia. The fruit is the size of a large orange, obscurely six-sided, with a smooth, leathery skin that ranges from brownish yellow to red; within, it is divided into several chambers containing many thin, transparent vesicles of reddish, juicy pulp, each surrounding an angular, elongated seed. The fruit is eaten fresh, and the juice is the source of grenadine syrup, used in flavorings and liqueurs. Throughout the East, the pomegranate has since earliest times occupied a position of importance alongside the grape and the fig.

300379978.label: halide
300379978.scope: Binary compound formed from a halogen and another element.

300380045.label: mercuric chloride
300380045.scope: White, crystalline compound formerly used extensively as wood preservative, antiseptic and disinfectant, insecticide, and, in archival conservation, a fungicide for paper and books. Due to its toxicity mercuric chloride's use is now restricted in the U.S.

300380102.label: russet (coarse fabric)
300380102.scope: Coarse homespun cloth, usually reddish or brownish in color.

300380162.label: vegetables
300380162.scope: Plants that are cultivated for food, typically restricted to the edible parts of a herbaceous plant (such as leaves, stems, or roots) that are traditionally served as a savory course of a meal.

300380203.label: myrrh
300380203.scope: Aromatic, yellow gum resin obtained from various African, Arabian, and Indian trees of the Commiphora genus. Myrrh contains approximately 25% resin (mostly triterpenoids), 60% gum, and 15% volatile oils. Translucent yellow resins have been used for incense and perfumes since ancient times. Myrrh has also been used for its healing properties in traditional medicines.

300380354.label: rabbit skin
300380354.scope: Skins of rabbits, usually including fur, used for apparel or other purposes.

300380405.label: frankincense (gum resin)
300380405.scope: Aromatic gum resin containing a volatile oil that was valued since ancient times in worship, as a medicine, and as an incense resin. It is obtained from the Boswellia sacra trees and others. It contains resins (mostly triterpenoids), gums, volatiles oils (pinene, dipentene), and bassorin. It is usually found in the form of hard yellow grains.

300386116.label: snipes
300386116.scope: General term for various species in the family Scolopacidae, characterized by having a long straight bill, and by frequenting marshy places.

300386154.label: unidentified (information indicator)
300386154.scope: General term referring to a person, people, place, or thing for which the identity has not been established .

300386505.label: rock salt
300386505.scope: Sodium chloride that occurs naturally as, or obtained mechanically from, a mineral deposit and sold as large crystals. Rock salt is used to melt ice, as a food preservative, and for the production of soda ash by the glass industry. To refer to the mineral composed of sodium chloride, use "halite."

300386648.label: weights and measures (general, standards)
300386648.scope: General term referring to systems of quantities taken as unified standards of measure, usually represent a uniform system established by a nation. The regulation of weights and measures is necessary for science, industry, and commerce.

300386691.label: greenstone (rock)
300386691.scope: Any of various rocks that are green in color, including altered igneous rocks colored green by feldspar, hornblende, augite, nephrite, or other minerals, or low-grade metamorphic rock containing actinolite, epidote, or albite. Greenstone has been used for carving and construction.

300386705.label: Curcuma longa (species)
300386705.scope: Species of  perennial, rhizomatous, herbaceous plant native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, valued for its root-stock, which is used as a spice, as a yellow dye, as a chemical test for alkalinity, and also medicinally.

300386730.label: spices
300386730.scope: Aromatic vegetative products such as ginger root, black pepper, and nutmeg, added to food as a flavoring or condiment.

300386877.label: lime plaster
300386877.scope: A type of plaster composed of calcium oxide (lime). Lime plaster has been used since antiquity, prepared by heating limestone to remove carbon dioxide and convert it to anhydrous calcium oxide (quicklime). When quicklime is mixed with water, it converts to calcium hydroxide (slaked lime).

300387147.label: rolling (preparation for storage and transporting)
300387147.scope: The process of wrapping a flat, flexible work or material around a cylinder or onto itself for the purpose of storage or transport. Examples include the following: the rolling of scrolls around a rod or onto themselves; the rolling of drawn, painted, printed, or inscribed works on parchment, paper, or canvas; the rolling of textiles, film, or other flexible works or materials.

300387541.label: Aloe (genus)
300387541.scope: Genus of  shrubby succulent plants in the family Asphodelaceae, containing hundreds of species native to Africa, Madagascar, and the Arabian Peninsula.

300389657.label: laths (wood by form)
300389657.scope: Thin, narrow, flat pieces of wood used for many purposes, such as in constructing lattices of trellis work, Venetian blinds, or to form a groundwork upon which to fasten the slates or tiles of a roof or the plaster of a wall or ceiling. For groundwork of any material upon which plaster or another such material is applied, use "lath (grounding surface)."

300389694.label: borers (tools)
300389694.scope: Tools, usually having a straight or tapered shank, designed for piercing, perforating, or making or enlarging a hole, especially when piercing by means of a rotatory movement; common examples include tools for boring through rocks or through wood. For tools used for piercing or making holes, but having a fluted or spiral shank, use "drills (tools)."

300389811.label: chemicals (materials)
300389811.scope: General term for distinct substances or compounds, having constant chemical composition and characteristic properties; usually refering to such substances that have been purified or prepared.

300389812.label: flour
300389812.scope: Material comprising the finer portion of grain meal, whether from wheat or another grain, that is separated by bolting.

300389813.label: meat
300389813.scope: The flesh of animals used as food.

300389819.label: butter
300389819.scope: The fatty substance obtained from cream by churning; used chiefly for spreading on bread and in cookery.

300389824.label: pepper (spice)
300389824.scope: The fruit of Piper nigrum, the pepper plant, dried and typically ground into powder to use as a condiment. It has a hot, pungent flavor and is most frequently paired with some form of salt. The ground spice appears in two forms, the more pungent black pepper, produced from black peppercorns, and the milder white pepper, produced from white peppercorns.

300389825.label: fish (meat)
300389825.scope: The flesh of fish used as food.

300389829.label: pastry
300389829.scope: Stiff dough made from flour, salt, and fat; usually in the form of butter, and some liquid. Also collectively, articles of food of which pastry forms an essential part, specifically pies or tarts after being baked.

300389919.label: citrons (fruits)
300389919.scope: Ovate acidic, juicy tree-fruits with a pale yellow rind. The citron is yellow in color, but larger, less acidic, and has a thicker rind than the lemon. Formerly the term included the lemons and the limes, as well as the fruits to which it is now restricted.

300390514.label: cheese
300390514.scope: Edible substance consisting of the curd of milk (coagulated by rennet), separated from the whey, and pressed into a solid mass.

300390542.label: Brassica (genus)
300390542.scope: Genus of plants including food crops such as cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, Brussels sprouts, and some types of seeds, including mustard.

300390955.label: chapes (weapon components)
300390955.scope: The metal plates or mountings of a scabbard or sheath; particularly those that cover the point.

300391258.label: holy cards
300391258.scope: Small prints, often on stiff paper, having a Christian theme. Holy cards often bear the image of Jesus, Mary, or a saint on one side, and a prayer or commemoration, as for a deceased person, on the reverse side. They are often collected or used as bookmarks in missals.

300391302.label: communion wafers
300391302.scope: Hosts, which are pieces of consecrated bread in Christian liturgies, that are small, very thin, and wafer-like, typically round with a meaningful Christian symbol stamped upon them. They are created in a special wafer iron. Communion wafers have been common in the western churches for hundreds of years. The first reference to small, round hosts, but not necessarily as thin as wafers, is mentioned in the eighth century; the small, regular hosts were seen as advantageous in eliminating the need to break up a piece of bread that could crumble easily. Eventually the hosts became very thin wafers that were widely adopted in the west. With the Second Vatican Council of the Roman Catholic Church, other forms of bread have again become increasingly common for consecration as hosts, as a reference to the original, ancient Christian practices.

300391379.label: ointment
300391379.scope: A medicinal or cosmetic preparation, in the form of a viscous or semisolid paste, applied to the skin; formerly used for ceremonial or sacramental anointing.

300393162.label: charger plates
300393162.scope: Large dinner plates, typically decorative and measuring 10-13 inches in diameter, that are placed on a formal dining table prior to dinner participants being seated and before food is served. The service plate remains at the place setting, with the bowls and plates of the dinner service placed on top of it, until the main entré is served, or until dessert is served; service plate use and etiquette varies by location and time period. For ceramic or metal platters for serving the meat course, use "chargers (platters)."

300395532.label: pelts (animal skins)
300395532.scope: Hides or skins that have been stripped from a dead animal, with hair, wool, or feathers attached; the legs, tail, and head may also be attached. For skins with hair that are used as a material, prefer "pelt (animal material)." For pelts mounted and represented as a three-dimensional animal, use "taxidermy mounts."

300395579.label: sheep shears
300395579.scope: Hand held cutting devices similar to scissors, designed to cut the woolen fleece from sheep. The earliest examples date to Bronze Age Crete.

300395593.label: splitting-spring locks
300395593.scope: Locks of various designs that are key operated or keyless letter-combination type, originating in China. When they are locked, the sliding bolt is trapped by the opening springs against the inner wall of the lock-body. They are often decorative objects as well as utilitarian.

300395637.label: siths (Flemish scythes)
300395637.scope: Reaping tools with L-shaped wooden handles and a blade. Siths allowed the user to stand upright, holding the crop with the mathook in the left hand, and cutting the crop with the sith in the right, which was different than with scythes.

300395639.label: silver thread
300395639.scope: Fiber or fiber-like material made wholly or in part from silver.

300395680.label: eggs (biological bodies)
300395680.scope: Bodies, typically tending to spheroidal shapes, that are produced by the female of birds, reptiles, fish, amphibians, and other animal species. Eggs are the organic vessels in which an animal embryo develops enclosed within a shell or membrane. For the egg cells of mammals and other animals, use "ova."

300400464.label: tusks (animal component)
300400464.scope: Long pointed teeth, particularly such teeth that project beyond the mouth, as in the elephant, wild boar, and various other animals. Tusks are generally seen in living mammals, but existed in other extinct animals. Tusks are used by the animal for mating competition, display, defense, offensive fighting, digging, and occasionally for hunting.

300400469.label: seeds (plant components)
300400469.scope: The characteristic reproductive bodies of both angiosperms (flowering plants) and gymnosperms (conifers, cycads, and ginkgos) and the ovary that encloses it. A seed consists of a miniature undeveloped plant (the embryo), which, alone or in the company of stored food for its early development after germination, is surrounded by a protective coat (the testa). Seeds are frequently small in size and suited to perform a wide variety of functions, such as multiplication, perennation (surviving seasons of stress such as winter), dormancy (a state of arrested development), and dispersal.

300400474.label: feathers (animal components)
300400474.scope: The component structures of the outer covering and flight surfaces of all modern birds and some dinosaurs, apparently having evolved from the scales of reptilian ancestors. The many different types of feathers are variously specialized for insulation, flight, formation of body contours, display, and sensory reception. The typical feather consists of a central shaft (rachis), with serial paired branches (barbs) forming a flattened, usually curved surface (the vane). The barbs possess further branches, the barbules.

300400480.label: roots (plant components)
300400480.scope: In botany, the parts of a plant normally underground, having the primary functions of anchorage of the plant, absorption of water and dissolved minerals and conduction of these to the stem, and storage of reserve foods.

300400557.label: dried flowers
300400557.scope: Flowers, often with stems attached, and other plants that are treated so as to remove moisture and in order to preserve them. Methods of drying flowers include hanging to dry, covering with a desiccant such as glycerin and silica, or pressing between paper, a textile, or another absorbent, wicking material.

300400561.label: gold thread
300400561.scope: Fiber or fiber-like material made wholly or in part from gold

300400594.label: mockado
300400594.scope: Fabric with a short woolen pile, usually of mohair, and resembling velvet. Used to produce tapestries, upholstery of soft furnishings, and formal dress.

300400695.label: clarions (historical aerophones)
300400695.scope: Valveless brass aerophones with conical bores. These were used mostly in the military to give signals to the infantry. Now chiefly used to refer to trumpet-like instruments of this kind in the Middle Ages and Renaissance, distinguished from modern "bugles."

300400751.label: terrets
300400751.scope: Metal loops attached to a horse's bit, which guide the reins and prevent them from becoming tangled or snagged on the harness.

300400785.label: soles (shoe components)
300400785.scope: The undersurfaces of shoes, boots, or other footwear that make contact with the ground; the parts upon which the wearer treads. These are usually made from firm but flexible materials such as rubber or leather.

300400792.label: calamine (pharmaceutical)
300400792.scope: A pharmaceutical substance made of zinc oxide with small amount of fenic oxide (to give faint pink color), and containing after ignition, not less than 98% and not more than 100.5% zinc oxide. Commercial calamine may be distributed as a pink lotion, used as a skin protectant and salve.

300400827.label: raw silk (textile)
300400827.scope: Textile made from untreated silk fibers as reeled from cocoons.

300400883.label: cinnabar (pigment)
300400883.scope: Pigment made from the mineral cinnabar, composed of mercuric sulfide. Cinnabar was finely ground for use as an artist pigment since antiquity. Red mercuric sulfide has been made synthetically since at least the 8th century in Europe and possibly earlier in China. Synthetic mercuric sulfide is called vermilion, favored over ground cinnabar as a red pigment because cinnabar, when exposed to ultraviolet light, darkens from its normal red crystalline form to a black isomorph, resulting in splotchy discolorations.

300400886.label: fillets (headgear)
300400886.scope: Ribbons, strings, or narrow bands of any material used for binding the hair, or worn round the head to keep the headdress in position, or simply for ornament.

300403912.label: gabardine
300403912.scope: Variety of twill-woven cloth, usually of fine worsted yarn or thread.

300404125.label: natural objects
300404125.scope: Objects that occur in nature, not made by humans. Used primarily in the context of distinguishing man-made objects from natural objects.

300404136.label: ceremonial robe
300404136.scope: Robes worn for ceremonial or official occasions, usually with significant details of trim or color.

300404203.label: black earth (pigment)
300404203.scope: A class of pigments where a variety of both inorganic and organic compounds may be present. Historically, comparatively little is known about which materials were used as black pigments, and in treatises on painting technique, the terms black earth, black chalk and black stone were used interchangeably, whether discussing black pigments or drawing materials. In current technical literature, black earth is generally assumed to be a black shale or chalk, but other bituminous materials and minerals have been identified.

300404235.label: sacristy bells
300404235.scope: Small to medium-sized clapper bells, usually mounted in a fixture extending from the wall at the sacristy door of a Christian church, rung to announce the entrance procession of the liturgical celebrants.

300404292.label: buskins (general footwear)
300404292.scope: Calf-high or knee-high boots or light coverings for the foot and leg, typically made from cloth or leather. May be made of decorated silk or other fine fabric; may fit inside a shoe like a stocking; sometimes forming part of the regalia of a monarch or eccesiastic.

300404293.label: almonds (drupe kernels)
300404293.scope: Oval, oil-rich kernels from the tree genus Prunus, having a light brown skin and a hard pitted shell, most varieties of which are edible.

300404294.label: candied fruit
300404294.scope: Fruits or pieces of fruits that are preserved by being impregnated with sugar.

300404380.label: comfits
300404380.scope: Tiny sweetmeats made of breath-freshening seeds such as caraway, coriander, or anis, or fruit or root, coated and preserved with sugar.

300404430.label: capacity (size measurement)
300404430.scope: The measure of the possible full content of a vessel or other container, if it were filled with liquid, grain, or other substance. For example, the capacity of a bottle could be one liter. For the measure of the mass of an object, use "volume."

300404445.label: packages
300404445.scope: The compilation of an object or group of objects packed, wrapped up, or tied together, generally restricted to relatively small or medium- sized compilations of objects. May refer to physical objects and also to digital objects.

300404446.label: packets (object compilations)
300404446.scope: Small compilations of things that are bound or packed together. For the bag or envelope for packing small compilations of things, use "packets (containers)." An example of a packet is the stack of gold called a "mold" compiled at one stage of the gold beating process.

300404831.label: rosewater
300404831.scope: Water distilled from roses or scented with essence of roses, used as a perfume, scenting a room, flavoring, in medicinal preparations, or for other purposes.

300404880.label: medicines (material)
300404880.scope: Substances, usually taken internally or applied topically, having the primary purpose of curing or alleviating symptoms of illness or injury.

300404900.label: dishes (object genre)
300404900.scope: Genre of objects having the form of a broad shallow container, with a flat bottom, concave sides, and nearly level rim, made of earthenware, glass, metal, wood, plastic, bone, or other materials, used for food, cosmetics, storage, transmission equipment, and for other purposes.

300410374.label: siphons (tubes)
300410374.scope: Devices comprising a tube or pipe, often bent with one end placed in a container or reservoir of liquid, such as a bottle or basin, and the other end outside it at a lower level. The aim is to convey liquid upwards from the container and out from the lower end of the pipe or tube. The liquid is conveyed through differences in atmospheric pressure on the liquid in the upper container that pushes it into the tube as gravity pulls downwards the liquid in the lower length of tubing; another force that accounts for the rise of the liquid up the tube has been attributed to the cohesiveness or tensile strength of the moving liquid rather than to atmospheric pressure.

300411341.label: woven material
300411341.scope: General term for materials comprising fibers or other components that are created by weaving. Includes, but not limited to, woven textiles.

300411352.label: hazelnuts (nuts)
300411352.scope: Nuts from any of about 15 species of shrubs and trees constituting the genus Corylus in the birch family (Betulaceae).

300411356.label: raisins
300411356.scope: Grapes that are partially dried in sunlight or by artificial means. Uses include eating as is, as an ingredient in cooking, and in the production of wine

300411364.label: enema syringes
300411364.scope: Instruments designed for the purpose of administering a liquid or gaseous substance into the rectum.

300411892.label: Salix viminalis (species)
300411892.scope: Multistemmed shrub typically found in wet environments near ponds or streams. It may grow from 10 to 20 feet high, and has long branches with green or gray bark and long, narrow leaves. Native range extends from Europe to Asia, but is cultivated widely. The tough pliant branches are commonly used in basketwork.

300412070.label: ells (units of length)
300412070.scope: Units of length, now obsolete, used in several European countries. In England, one ell corresponded to approximately 45 inches. In Scotland, 37.2 inches. The Flemish ell corresponded to 27 inches.

300412103.label: poison
300412103.scope: Material that causes illness or death when absorbed, inhaled, or ingested by a living organism; particularly when the substance is able to kill by rapid action and when taken in small quantity. For a toxic material secreted by an animal and injected into a victim, use "venom."

300417251.label: Agaricomycetes (class)
300417251.scope: Mushroom-forming; parenthesomes imperforate or perforate (spore caps have openings); includes subclasses Agaricomycetidae and Phallomycetidae; contains 17 orders.

300417315.label: fur garments
300417315.scope: Costume of any kind, made primarily or entirely of fur.

300417335.label: prunes (dried fruit)
300417335.scope: The dried or partially dried fruit of the plum tree.

300417719.label: whale bone (bone)
300417719.scope: Material comprising the bone of whales.

300417726.label: bundles
300417726.scope: Collections of things bound or otherwise fastened or bound together.

300417859.label: waste silk
300417859.scope: The spinnable fibers resulting from processing silk; damaged cocoons, waste caused by searching for the beginning of a continuous filament while reeling silk, or the inner section of a cocoon out of which moths have been allowed to escape. When spun, this yarn is less lustrous than filament silk yarn. It is mostly used as warp or weft in a fabric, or for products such as ribbon and sewing thread.

300417959.label: melting pots
300417959.scope: Vessels in which metals or other materials are melted and mixed.

300417970.label: vestments (general ceremonial costume)
300417970.scope: General term for ceremonial costume worn by kings, pelates, sacrificial victims, or other people for religious or other ceremonial or ritual purposes.

300419317.label: pine resin
300419317.scope: Exudate of pine trees, used for a variety of purposes, including as a sealant, incense, and in ancient Egypt, for embalming and preserving human bodies.

300419344.label: pavilions (tents)
300419344.scope: Large, stately, or ornamental tents or tent-like coverings, usually rising to a central point rather than a ridge. Originally referred to tents used on military campaigns or at jousts.

300419352.label: Cinnamomum cassia (species)
300419352.scope: An evergreen tree native to southern China, and cultivated elsewhere in southern and eastern Asia. It is prized for its aromatic bark, which is commonly used as the spice cinnamon, though it is not true cinnamon, and as an environmentally-friendly insecticide in the context of conservation.

300419363.label: Martes foina (species)
300419363.scope: Martes foina, more commonly known as stone martens or beech martens, are found across Europe, and Central Asia. They are weasel-like carnivores that are more generally found in deciduous forests or on rocky hillsides.

300419451.label: drinks
300419451.scope: Any liquid that may be ingested for assuaging thirst, or as nourishment. For prepared or flavored liquids drunk as refreshment, or for pleasure, including alcoholic drinks, but excluding plain water, use 'beverages,' though these concepts overlap in meaning and usage.

300419970.label: fiberworking tools
300419970.scope: Tools or equipment for working fibers, generally restricted to fibers other than textile fibers.

300421395.label: cage traps
300421395.scope: Animal traps that lure or allow a target animal to enter inside an enclosure, but prevents the target animal from exiting once trapped. Cage traps exist in a variety of designs and sizes; they are used for hunting and to live-capture animals for relocation or other purposes.

300421448.label: caltrops
300421448.scope: Snares that catch the feet of animals in hunting or trapping, or in the context of warfare.

300421505.label: bed mats
300421505.scope: Protective coverings on which a mattress or bedroll can be laid, for protection or comfort.

300422672.label: carding combs
300422672.scope: Specialized combs, typically made of wood, comprising a flat surface covered by iron nails, wire teeth, or other sharp objects designed to manually disentangible the fibres from textile materials prior to spinning.

300422727.label: carrying baskets
300422727.scope: Containers made of woven plant material of varying shape. Some examples contain lids or hoops for carrying poles. Made to carry various personal materials.

300423311.label: bolts (cloth)
300423311.scope: Lengths of woven or knitted cloth, typically measuring approximately 40 to 100 yards long, folded or rolled on a cylindrical or rectangular core. Often stored in an upright position on shelves or racks and wrapped in plastic or other protective material to prevent damage, these fabric rolls are used to create myriad textile products. They can be made of cotton, silk, wool, or synthetic fibers, depending on desired use.

300423334.label: clothing clasps
300423334.scope: Fastenings that hold together parts of garments.

300423365.label: coal shovels
300423365.scope: Metal scoops of varied size used to gather or transport coal.

300424099.label: crossbow bolts (edged weapons)
300424099.scope: Dart-like projectiles intended to be launched by crossbows. These are generally shorter and have greater weight than arrows shot from bows.

300424213.label: cushion covers
300424213.scope: Sleeves of textile or other material such as plastic, into which upholstered cushions are inserted for protection from soil or wear.

300425514.label: fireplace accessories
300425514.scope: Implements used in or around a fireplace to kindle, stoke, maintain, or otherwise tend to a fire and its remains.

300425538.label: firkins
300425538.scope: Small casks containing a quarter of a barrel or half a kilderkin for liquids, fish, butter, or other foods.

300426133.label: holy water vessels
300426133.scope: General term for containers made to hold water consecrated by a priest or other religious figure. Examples include holy water fonts located outside of Christian churches.

300426934.label: hand cards
300426934.scope: Manual wool carders used in the spinning of cotton, wool, and other natural fibers. These hand-held devices are typically made of sharp wire or steel teeth adhered to layered leather and mounted on rectangular wooden frames a thin handles. To carry out the manual carding process, users hold a card in each hand with the teeth pointing towards each other. Wool or other fibers are placed between both cards, which are dragged lightly over the wool to disentangle and smooth the fibers.

300426959.label: hand towels
300426959.scope: Small towels or cloths used to dry hands after washing them.

300427074.label: hawsers
300427074.scope: Large ropes or small cables midway between the size of a cable or a tow-line, and 5 to10 inches in circumference; used in warping and mooring.

300428728.label: packs
300428728.scope: Bags or containers of varied form designed to carry objects by one person.

300429605.label: notions
300429605.scope: A broad category of small wares, especially cheap, useful articles, specifically for haberdashery or sewing; buttons, hooks, ribbon, and thread.

300429634.label: nut shellers
300429634.scope: Mechanical devices for removing the shells from nuts.

300430046.label: roasting jacks
300430046.scope: Mechanical devices used to turn spits or hooks in order to evenly roast meat over a fire.

300432212.label: shoe buckles
300432212.scope: Fasteners attached to shoes, used for both decoration and to secure shoes to the wearer.

300432641.label: water casks
300432641.scope: Strong light casks used for transporting and dispensing drinking-water, often in the context of ships at sea or where potable is not otherwise available.

300433379.label: yarn reels
300433379.scope: Devices designed to support a skein of yarn while it is being unwound during use and/or wound into a ball for future use. These devices traditionally comprised a circular board nailed to a piece of oak to be handled manually, but are now electric and equipped with automated pre-selection counters for setting the desired yarn length.

300433870.label: stills (culinary equipment)
300433870.scope: Apparatuses for distillation, consisting essentially of a closed vessel (alembic, retort, or boiler) in which the substance to be distilled is subjected to the action of heat, and of arrangements for the condensation of the vapor produced.

300434240.label: syringes
300434240.scope: Cylindrical instruments, most often consisting of a tube mounting a piston, or a tube with a rubber bulb attached, used to draw in liquid, and to eject it in a stream or jet for making injections, taking samples, cleansing, or for other purposes.

300434261.label: table mats
300434261.scope: Removable mats found in a variety of fabrics, shapes, and patterns that are generally embroidered. Used under vases or dishes to protect the table from wear, or for decoration.

300434264.label: table runners
300434264.scope: Long narrow strips of cloth placed along a table for decoration or to protect the surface when placing objects upon it.

300434558.label: tenterhooks
300434558.scope: Small metal spikes or hooks designed to secure and stretch the edges of wet woven cloth as it dries after being exposed to fabrication processes such as washing, beating, and fulling, amongst others. Hundreds of these hooks are positioned in close rows around a wooden tenter frame to hold the fabric taut and prevent the damp piece of cloth from shrinking and warping out of shape during the drying process. Widely used in Europe beginning in the 15th century, this term's meaning later evolved and was abstracted in the 16th century to mean the expansion of one's consciousness and uncertainty about one's future.

300434583.label: textile combs
300434583.scope: Hand-held devices fitted with a series of metal teeth, which are designed to eliminate neps and impurities in fibers, as well as to ensure that fibers lay parallel to one another. While these devices can take many forms, they are typically utilized to create cleaner, finer, stronger, and more lustrous fibers.

300434639.label: thimble cases
300434639.scope: Enclosing containers of varied design, used for storing thimbles for needlework.

300434662.label: threshers
300434662.scope: Equipment or machines that are used to separate grain from the straw by beating with a flail, or otherwise.

300435019.label: sailmaker's needles
300435019.scope: Triangular-sectioned and heavy guage needles with softened edges traditionally used for hand-sewing sails.

300435103.label: falconry
300435103.scope: The sport or activity involving chasing or hunting game using a trained bird of the family Falconidae, usually a hawk.

300435300.label: Apiaceae (family)
300435300.scope: Family of flowering plants comprising between 300 and 400 genera of plants distributed principally in the north temperate regions. Most members are aromatic herbs with alternate, feather-divided leaves that are sheathed at the base. The flowers are often arranged in a conspicuous umbel (a flat-topped cluster of flowers). Many species are poisonous.

300435312.label: spatulas (general tools)
300435312.scope: Implements having a flat elongated form with various modifications of shape and size, used for a variety of purposes, such as mixing, stirring, spreading, lifting, or examining.

300435353.label: pears
300435353.scope: The pome fruit of a tree (genus Pyrus, especially P. communis) that typically has a pale green or brownish skin, a firm juicy flesh, and an oblong shape in which a broad base end tapers upward to a narrow stem end.

300435586.label: Gentiana (genus)
300435586.scope: Genus containing around 400 species of annual or perennial (rarely biennial) flowering plants, distributed worldwide in temperate and alpine regions, especially in Europe and Asia, North and South America, and New Zealand.

300435605.label: Zingiberaceae (family)
300435605.scope: Family of flowering plants containing around 52 genera and more than 1,300 species.

300435606.label: Curcuma (genus)
300435606.scope: Genus of around 100 species of flowering plants native to Southeast Asia, southern China, the Indian Subcontinent, New Guinea, and northern Australia.

300439889.label: jewels
300439889.scope: Valuable man-made objects often made of precious metals and gemstones. Any object of this sort used as an ornament or personal adornment set with stones or decorated with enamel and worn as an accessory of dress.

300440738.label: onions (bulbs)
300440738.scope: Edible rounded bulbs of Allium cepa, which consist of fleshy concentric leaf-bases. Onions have a strong pungent flavour and smell, and vary in color from white to yellow and dark red, and are used as a culinary vegetable throughout the world, eaten raw, cooked, or pickled.

300440763.label: hangers (mounting equipment)
300440763.scope: Any of various hardware or non-structural contrivances by which an object is hung from a wall or other surface.

300443564.label: marblers (generic craftspeople)
300443564.scope: General term for those who create marbled surfaces by imitating or suggesting the appearance or pattern of marble or another such stone, usually by hand painting on paper, wood, fresco, or other surfaces.

300443573.label: writing materials
300443573.scope: Materials or substrates on which something is inscribed, such as paper or parchment.

300444098.label: neck pieces (armor components)
300444098.scope: Pieces of armor that cover or protect the neck of the human or animal wearer.

300444361.label: cereals
300444361.scope: Collectively describes plants or grasses which are cultivated as food crops. These may include wheat, rye, barley, oats, millet, rice, and maize. For the edible seeds of these plants use 'grain.'

300448623.label: dates (fruits)
300448623.scope: Edible fruits of the date palm; oblong drupes with a single hard seed and sweet pulp. An important food crop in North Africa and western Asia.

300448624.label: figs (fruits)
300448624.scope: Fruits of the fig tree. Figs are syconia, inflorescences formed by an enlarged, fleshy, hollow receptacle with multiple ovaries on the inside surface. Figs are borne singly or in pairs above the scars of fallen leaves or in axils of leaves of the present season.

300451394.label: hand barrows
300451394.scope: Flat frames or shallow boxes used for transporting materials over short distances. These are generally dependent on two people to move.

300456642.label: ale (beverage)
300456642.scope: A type of fermented malt beverage that is fermented rapidly at high temperature; fermentation is checked while a considerable portion of sugar still remains unchanged.

300456708.label: lures
300456708.scope: Apparatuses used for alluring animals to be captured.
